Title: BIRMINGHAM Indoor Climbing - MONDAY - Beginners
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for an evening at Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre.
*** Beginner (supervised) events are not offered every week ***
If you have never climbed before (or need a refresher on the basics), then this BEGINNERS EVENT is ideal for you! We will happily show you the ropes & teach you everything you need to know to climb safely!
Event pages are split into
BEGINNER & EXPERIENCED.
Please ensure you sign up to the correct event as we can only supervise two beginners at once per leader.
This event is for beginner climbers (those needing to be supervised) only!
If you are competent with how to tie in & belay (safely & confidently), then you will need to
sign up to the accompanying experienced (independent climber) event
instead.
If you are climbing with us for the first time, whether Experienced or Beginner, it is essential that you send a note to the Event Leader telling them about your previous climbing experience & your goals!
Bouldering
- Most of us do roped climbing, but if you prefer to do bouldering, you can sign yourself in & go bouldering (unsupervised) instead of, or as well as, roped climbing. Please meet the leader & the group at the start though; some others might wish to do bouldering too!
Please note that we will not teach lead climbing or lead belaying on this event -
we would suggest having some
lessons in Lead Climbing
by a qualified member of staff if this is something you're interested in pursuing!
If you are subsequently unable to attend, please cancel off the event. Spaces for beginners are limited & 'no-shows' are not only rude, but also frustrating for the leader & other attendees who may have travelled over an hour away to climb with you!
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
Indoor climbing centres offer the challenges of climbing that you'll find on natural rock crags - simply indoors! It's a fun way to stay fit, make new friends & develop your climbing skills.
Climbing
- Unlike Indoor Bouldering there is a certain amount of skill to be mastered, such as tying in knots & belaying a partner, as well as the climbs being higher than in bouldering. If you are new to climbing (or would like a refresher), there are plenty of top-rope routes to choose from after learning the essential climbing & safety techniques with one of our friendly, experienced climbing leaders.
Bouldering
- Instead of tackling long high routes, the 'problems' (as they are referred to) are shorter & focus on technique, balance, body positioning & sometimes power. With the different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, so it’s excellent (but not necessarily easier) for newcomers.
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
has more than 75 lines with over 300 routes, set through some spectacular ground including its notorious 'stalactite'. It even features one of the few indoor 'Yorkshire VS cracks' in the country, to test your jamming skills. The bouldering rooms are just as interesting as its climbing routes, over 200 bouldering problems have been organised into graded circuits to provide something for everyone.
You MUST register via this event page before coming to the centre!

Title: Bouldering NORTH WALES - Beginners welcome
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads For An Evening of INDOOR BOULDERING in NORTH WALES!
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Bouldering is a form of climbing that focuses on shorter "problems" emphasising technique, balance, body positioning, and sometimes power, rather than long, high routes. Without the need for ropes, harnesses, and belaying, bouldering is an accessible activity for newcomers and is often considered the "purest" form of climbing.
Bouldering offers a wide range of benefits, including:
Physical:
Improved strength, tone, balance, power, and coordination.
Mental:
Enhanced problem-solving, focus, concentration, and body awareness.
Emotional:
Relaxation, a sense of achievement, and a feeling of mind-body connection.
Bouldering is also a fantastic way to meet new people and build lasting friendships, as it's an inherently social sport where climbers share tips and strategies to conquer the routes.
New to Bouldering?
If you're new to bouldering, it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader to learn the basics of safe bouldering. The leader can then introduce you to the rest of the group where you can refine your newly learnt skills in a social environment.
Experienced Boulderer?
If you’re new to climbing with ODL, the leader will help to introduce you to the rest of the group so you can explore the centre together.
You are responsible for your own safety and actions while bouldering. Please use your own judgement when accepting advice from OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers, regardless of your bouldering experience.
Ready to boulder?
You will need to sign up on the ODL event page. We would ask you to do this each time so that the leader has access to important information
If you are not already registered with The Boardroom Climbing centre you will need to do so when you arrive. Maybe arrive a little earlier to do so.
When you arrive at the centre you will need to pay for entry and hire climbing shoes if you don't own a pair.
Get bouldering! You’ll find most of the group already bouldering so feel free to join them. If you’re new to bouldering with ODL, the leader will be looking out for you so if you spot them, please go speak with them first.
Any questions?
If you have any questions, please contact the leader directly.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by Mark Mckee
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: Experienced Climbing Evening
Summary:
Fancy an evening of climbing with a great bunch of OutdoorLads?
Join us at
Beacon Climbing Centre in Caernarfon
for an evening of climbing, training and socialising. This event is aimed at
experienced climbers
who are comfortable climbing without supervision and want to enjoy some indoor climbing with other OutdoorLads members.
We'll spend the evening making the most of Beacon's excellent climbing facilities, with a mixture of climbing, bouldering and generally having a good time.
The evening is intended to be relaxed and sociable rather than a formal coached session. There should be plenty of opportunity to climb with different people, swap tips and meet other OutdoorLads members who enjoy climbing.
This event is aimed at experienced climbers.
You should be confident climbing without supervision and familiar with the relevant safety procedures and equipment for the type of climbing you intend to do.
This event is for OutdoorLads members who already have climbing experience and would like to meet up for an evening of climbing in a friendly, social environment.
Whether you're looking to get some training in, try some different routes, or simply have a climb and a chat with other members, you're very welcome.
Come along, get climbing and enjoy an evening with OutdoorLads!
Difficulty & Distance: This event is for EXPERIENCED climbers only!!!

Summary:
Taking in the best of Newcastle’s parks, bridges, creative quarter of Ouseburn this is roughly a six mile walk to see some of the prettier parts of Newcastle away from the City Centre. This will include Jesmond Dene, Armstrong Bridge, Heaton Park and the Ouseburn quarter.

Title: Indoor Climbing MANCHESTER - Beginners welcome!
Summary:
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Join us for an evening of climbing in one of the UK's top climbing centres. Whether you are new to climbing or a seasoned climber, this centre offers something for everyone with a huge selection of routes including top rope, lead and auto belay.
Prefer to boulder? That's well catered for as well, with an extensive modern bouldering area ensuring there is plenty to keep you busy, or you can swap between climbing and bouldering on the same night.
Climbing is the main focus of the event, but this is also a great chance to meet other members and build lasting friendships. Many Outdoor Lads members join through climbing, so if you're new to the group and want to know more, come along and chat over a cuppa during the tea and cake break.
What to expect on your first climb with us?
If you are an experienced climber and have passed the centre's proficiency test, we'll pair you up with a climbing buddy and you'll be out exploring the centre in no time.
If you have never climbed before or think you could do with a refresher, we offer supervised climbing sessions with one of our leaders, subject to availability. That session will focus on introducing you to climbing, making sure you get plenty of time on the wall whilst also showing you how to belay safely. Due to the centre's rules, we are limited in the number of climbers the leader is able to supervise in each session so if you think you may need a supervised session,
please contact the leader before signing up to make sure there is enough space.
As a general guide, if you answer "no" to any of the following questions, you should opt for a supervised session:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie into a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay and lower down another climber correctly and confidently?
After a few supervised sessions, you should be ready to complete the centre's proficiency test and once that has been passed, you'll be able to climb with the rest of the group.
Everything else you need to know
You will need to register with Big Depot before your first visit to the centre but you only need to do this once. If you are an experienced climber, you can save time and do this online
here
, selecting the 18+ unsupervised option. This also applies if you just want to boulder, just select the relevant options during the registration. If you are a beginner and require a supervised session, the leader will help register you when you are at the centre.
Photos provided by Sieh and Dexmonster.
Difficulty & Distance: There is a range of routes of varying difficulty, but there should be something to suit everybody

Title: Weald and Downland: Trek the Hills with Brows so Jolly!
Summary:
The afternoon of this event will comprise a visit to the Weald and Downland Living Museum. If you wish to do this, please purchase a ticket
here
at a cost of £14.90, and select the 13.00-14.00 entry slot.
During Advent, the Weald and Downland open-air museum near Chichester explores how people prepared for Christmas in earlier centuries. In the historic buildings there you'll find period-attired re-enactors demonstrating traditional crafts, food preparation and winter housekeeping. Advent was traditionally a period of preparation and fasting, with the Christmas decoration and feasting beginning on Christmas Day, so the museum doesn't turn the historic houses into Christmas grottoes, but this visit to the museum will still overflow with festivity and fellowship. We'll walk deep into and high-up in the South Downs National Park at its loveliest, but we'll return by bus to the starting point.
My thanks go to the lovely Josh Zarn for suggesting this event.
The sights:
Chichester:
A cathedral city of Roman origin (Noviomagus Reginorum) founded soon afer the Claudian invasion of 43 AD. Many Georgian buildings and a thriving arts scene. The chief sights are:
City walls:
Originally Roman, c 200 AD, four metres wide and five metres high in places. 80 per cent complete, making them the most intact circuit of Roman town defences in Southern England;
Pallant House Gallery:
The original Pallant House was built 1712-13 is one of Chichester's finest Georgian houses. It is rather upstaged by the admittedly very fine Gallery of 2003-6 by Colin St John Wilson, architect of the British Library. The third design for this was eventually accepted after the first two were reviled;
South and North Pallant:
Attractive historic streets of C18 and early C19 town houses, predominantly in brick or stucco, with sash windows, classical doorcases, cornices and tiled roofs. Their varied façades and rooflines preserve the character of Georgian Chichester;
St Martin’s Street and St Martin’s Square:
A compact historic area containing C18 town houses with classical detailing, including rusticated ground floors, pilasters, cornices and pedimented doorways. No. 8 St Martin’s Square is particularly distinguished for its red-brick façade and central entrance.
East Lavant:
Beside the river with a lovely intricate yet relaxed plan. Brick, flint and thatched cottages and a superb view north to the Downs. St Mary's Church is C12 and C13 with a plain brick tower of 1671 and all the rest a Victorian restoration of 1863.
St Roche's Hill and the Trundle:
206 m in elevation. The Trundle (Old English 'Tryndel' or 'circle') is an Iron Age hill fort built around a Neolithic causewayed enclosure. Subsequent history involves a chapel to St Roche (lost), a Civil War encampment and a viewing area to Goodwood Racecourse. There are wonderful views to be had, north over the Weald and south over the Sussex Plain and the Sea.
Goodwood:
We won't see the late C18 stately home and we'll only see the aerodrome, car racing circuit and site of the Goodwood Revival at a distance, but we'll get a grandstand view of the grandstands of the famous racecourse. 'Glorious Goodwood' earned its honorific by being 180m up, and set in sublime countryside. It was laid out in 1801 as a private military racecourse. The current stands are the March Stand of 1980, the Charlton Stand of 1989 and the Sussex Stand of 1990, the latter by Arup Associates.
Singleton:
A small village in the Lavant Valley below the South Downs escarpment. Historic core of flint and brick cottages, tile-hung elevations and tiled roofs. St Mary’s Church retains an early C11 tower, with C13 nave and aisle arcades and C15 alterations. The surrounding downland and farmland offer a timeless rural setting.
Weald and Downland Living Museum, Singleton:
Open-air museum founded in 1970, occupying a 40-acre site on the South Downs. More than 50 historic buildings, dismantled at their original sites and re-erected here, illustrate vernacular architecture and rural life over a millennium. Includes medieval timber-framed houses, C17–C19 cottages, barns, workshops and a working watermill. Traditional materials and techniques include timber framing, wattle and daub, thatch, clay tiles and local stone. Especially valuable for presenting historic buildings within their original functional contexts.
The
route
(click the link to see the walk at the OS website)
:
Leaving the station we will cross the town centre along South and North Pallant, then through St Martin's Street and St Martin's Square to Priory Lane. At the top of New Park Road we'll cross Spitalfield Lane to walk north along College Lane out to Summersdale suburb. Beyond that, the West Sussex Literary Trail running along Fordwater Road will take us out of the town into the countryside to East Lavant to begin ascending the Downs by way of Chalk Pit Lane. At the top of the lane, we'll cross the Trundle, follow Knight's Hill towards Charlton before a footpath veers off towards Singleton. Walking west along Charlton Road and south along Town Road will bring us to the museum.
Getting the bus back
The Stagecoach no. 60 bus runs from outside the museum in Singleton to Chichester at 10 and 40 minutes past and costs £3.
Dogs:
I love having dogs on my walks and this walk is suitable for them, although there will be lots of road walking in town and may be some fields with livestock. Dogs are encouraged at the museum, but because of free-range lifestock there, they will have to be on a short lead of at most 1.2 m, and extendable or flexi-leads are not permitted. Dogs are also not permitted in a few buildings. A dog off the lead must be obedient.

Title: Boots, Beacon and Beer Walk
Summary:
Glynde & Firle Beacon Craft Beer Circular
Starting and finishing in
Glynde, East Sussex
, near Lewes, this circular walk is perfect for OutdoorLads who enjoy a good hike, spectacular South Downs scenery and a well-earned craft beer at the end!
Join us for a
small, friendly and intimate group walk
as we head out from Glynde and climb onto the South Downs. The walk gets off to a challenging start with a steep ascent, but the effort is soon rewarded with
stunning panoramic views across the Sussex countryside
.
We’ll make our way towards
Firle Beacon
, standing at 217 metres, taking in the rolling chalk hills, open downland and beautiful views along the way. We’ll also pass close to the impressive
Firle Place
, before completing our circular route back towards Glynde.
And, of course, no OutdoorLads walk for craft beer lovers would be complete without a
proper pub finale
! We finish the walk back at Glynde Train Station, home to the Steamworks Bar, where we can enjoy a few well-earned craft beers and swap stories from the day.
🥾 Walk highlights
Stunning South Downs views
– especially spectacular on a clear day
Firle Beacon
– climb to the 217m summit
Beautiful Sussex countryside
– rolling hills, chalk downs and picturesque villages
Firle Place
– one of the area's historic country estates
Challenging opening climb
– earn those views!
Craft beer pub finale
– the perfect reward after a day on the Downs 🍻
Bring your walking boots, plenty of water and your thirst for adventure...
Check out the route on
OS Maps
.
After the walk
The fun doesn’t have to end when the walking stops! We’ll head to Glynde Steamworks Bar at the railway station to enjoy a few well-earned pints and continue the good company. If you fancy some food afterwards, you can hop on the train into Lewes, where you’ll find a much wider choice of pubs, restaurants and places to grab a bite to eat.
Further Information
The Steamworks Bar has a sister bar located in Seaford and has recently featured in the
The Guardian 10 of the best railway station pubs in England
.
Difficulty & Distance: 10.5 miles - around 413 metres of total ascent.

Title: Indoor Climbing NORTH WALES - Beginners welcome
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads For An Evening of INDOOR CLIMBING in NORTH WALES!
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Join us for an evening of indoor climbing! Whether you are new to climbing or a seasoned climber, this centre offers something for everyone with a huge selection of routes.
While
climbing
will be the main focus of the event, the centre offer great
bouldering
problems too, so if that's more you're thing, then you're more than welcome to come along and just boulder. But this is also a great chance to meet other members and build lasting friendships. Many OutdoorLads members join through climbing, so if you're new to the group and want to know more, come along and chat over a cuppa during the tea and cake break.
What to expect on your first climb with us?
If you are an experienced climber and have passed the centre's proficiency test, we'll pair you up with a climbing buddy and you'll be out exploring the centre in no time.
If you have never climbed before or think you could do with a refresher, we offer supervised climbing sessions with one of our leaders, subject to availability. That session will focus on introducing you to climbing, making sure you get plenty of time on the wall whilst also showing you how to belay safely. Due to the centre's rules, we are limited in the number of climbers the leader is able to supervise in each session so if you think you may need a supervised session,
please contact the leader before signing up to make sure there is enough space.
As a general guide, if you answer "no" to any of the following questions, you will need to be supervised for the session:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie into a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay and lower down another climber correctly and confidently?
After a few supervised sessions, you should be ready to complete the centre's proficiency test and once that has been passed, you'll be able to climb with the rest of the group.
Everything else you need to know
You will need to register with
The Boardroom Climbing centre
before you start climbing. You only need to do this once and can be done on the day. This also applies if you just want to boulder, just select the relevant options during the registration. If you are a beginner and require a supervised session, the leader will help register you when you are at the centre.
Any questions?
If you have any questions, please contact the leader directly.

Title: Park Life and Pond Life - a County Durham Ramble
Summary:
Join Steven for a relaxed easier stroll in rural County Durham.
Setting off from the small town that once was visited by a former president of the USA we will head over close to a golf course and Country Park. This is a pleasant walk along paths and lanes through woodland by streams and ponds.
After a loop north of the Country Park we will head past a hotel and site of a popular summer festival and into the public park.  This area has seen huge improvements to when the walk leader first came here as a child.
We will walk around the larger lake and then to an impressive folly on the top of a rise giving a good panorama of the entire walk area today.
After joining a path around the Serpentine pools we will visit the café before the final short section to the town centre where we could stop to have a drink and hot food.
This walk is suitable for well behaved dogs, these should be kept under close control when near the many geese and ducks.
Please join Steven as he returns to the place he regularly visited as a young one many decades ago.

Title: An Autumnal Railway Ramble to Ramsbottom
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for a brilliant autumn day out in the borders of Greater Manchester and Lancashire! We’ll start with a nostalgic trip on the historic East Lancashire Heritage Railway from Bury to Ramsbottom, before heading out on a scenic circuit packed with iconic views, heritage, and great company.
Whether you're a regular or joining us for your very first OutdoorLads event, this walk offers a great mix of rolling countryside, wild moorland, and rich local history—a perfect day out to catch up with friends and meet new ones.
What to Expect
Historic Railway Journey: Kick off the day aboard the nostalgic East Lancashire Railway from Bury to Ramsbottom, enjoying scenic autumnal views along the Irwell Valley.
Riverside Stroll: Follow the peaceful path along the River Irwell, enjoying gentle waterside walking as we head toward the hills.
Stubbins Estate & Woodlands: Wander down through the beautiful autumnal woods and countryside paths of the National Trust Stubbins Estate.
Holcombe Moor Trek: Experience the open, fresh air of Holcombe Moor with scenic high-ground trails.
Peel Tower & Panoramic Vistas: Head up Holcombe Hill to the landmark Peel Tower for sweeping, spectacular views across Manchester, the West Pennines, and beyond.
Social Finish: Wrap up back in Ramsbottom with the option to grab a well-deserved post-walk drink or bite to eat at a cozy local pub with the group!
Key Details & Practicalities:
Distance & Elevation:
Approximately 8 miles with 414m total elevation gain.
Terrain
: Mix of riverside paths, woodland tracks, moorland trails, and a steady hill climb up to Peel Tower.
Atmosphere
: Relaxed, inclusive, and social—ideal for making connections in a supportive outdoor environment.
This is a dog friendly event - so please bring your pooches along !
Dogs are allowed to travel on the railway free of charge
, however they must be kept on a lead at all times

Title: Sheffield bouldering @ Depot Climbing
Summary:
Swap trainers for climbing shoes and join OutdoorLads for an evening of INDOOR BOULDERING at Depot Climbing in Sheffield.

If you haven't been to Depot Climbing before, please click

What is Bouldering?
It's a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes it an excellent activity for newcomers to the sport. No wonder it's often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
I'm new to Bouldering - can I come along?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
I've been Bouldering before?
As above, everyone attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you responsible for your own safety, actions and involvement at all times. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by the event leader / venue.
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with some experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.

Title: Vale of Llangollen
Summary:
Join Dan for a walk down his own memory lane back to his very first OutdoorLads event some 18 or so years ago!
From the car park we will follow the Llangollen Canal up the valley before climbing steeply up onto the panorama road, then steeper still up to Castell Dinas Bran, a ruined 13th Century castle with some truly stunning views down into the town itself and lower Vale.
Dropping down into Llangollen we cross the River Dee as it crashes dramatically through the town (maybe spotting some brave kayakers) and head out to the southern side of the valley, ascending up to the fields and eastwards on the Llywybr Ceiriog Trail.
As we reach Froncysyllte our route back to the car park crosses the "masterpiece of creative genius" that is Thomas Telford's Pontcysyllte Aqueduct. If you don't have a head of heights there is a slightly longer option that follows the road down to the valley floor and up the other side.

Title: No Footslog to the Spotted Dog - Another Kentish Castles Christmas Cracker
Summary:
A wintry Wealden walk where Yuletide cheer meets Tudor charm. We’ll visit Chiddingstone, one of England’s best-preserved Tudor villages, with its timber-framed houses and cobbled pavement, before crossing the lakeside grounds of Chiddingstone Castle, a Gothic-revival mansion. Footpaths and country lanes will then lead us through gentle farmland towards Smarts Hill, where we'll eat in the private dining room of The Spotted Dog pub. We’ll continue to Penshurst, whose magnificent medieval manor, Penshurst Place, has become the epitome of Elizabethan evocativeness. All in all, we might not be walking in a winter wonderland, but the band of brothers bonhomie will be brilliant.
The sights:
Chiddingstone:
A unique and perfect example of a Tudor one-street village, so perfect, that the whole place is in the care of the National Trust. It's quite a film star too, as it featured in the 1985 Merchant Ivory film
A Room With a View,
Michael Winner's 1983
The Wicked Lady
and the outdoor scenes of the BBC's 1971
Elizabeth R
, starring Glenda Jackson. St Mary's Church is opulent, C14 and C15, and has the tombs to the Streatfeild family (you may have heard of Noel, the author) who lived at early C19 Chiddingstone Castle. The village takes its name from the Chiding Stone, a Saxon judicial place or boundary marker and place of public correction or 'chiding'.
Penshurst:
The village occupies a sheltered position in the rolling Weald, its historic core clustered around the parish church and the approach to Penshurst Place. It retains a notably coherent group of timber-framed houses, cottages and later brick buildings, many with steeply pitched tiled roofs and projecting upper storeys. St John the Baptist’s church, set back from the street, is principally medieval, with C13 and C14 arcades and a fine Perpendicular west tower; its Victorian restoration was by George Gilbert Scott in 1864–65. The proximity of church and manor house gives the village an unusually strong historic character.
Penshurst Place:
A substantial, irregular manor house of sandstone, brick and ragstone, its picturesque silhouette enriched by battlements, towers and steep tiled roofs. The core is the great Baron’s Hall, built for Sir John de Pulteney in 1341, with an imposing chestnut roof and carved timber screen. A mid-C15 wing was followed by extensive Elizabethan additions, including a long gallery and the remodelled King’s Tower. Granted to the Sidney family by Edward VI in 1552, the house became their ancestral seat. C19 restoration by George Devey consolidated its Tudor character. The house stands amid formal walled gardens and a medieval deer park. It has been used for filming
Anne of the Thousand Days
(1969),
Elizabeth R
(1971),
The Princess Bride
(1987),
The Other Boleyn Girl
(2008),
Merlin
(2008),
Wolf Hall
(2015),
Mary Queen of Scots
(2018), and
Renegade Nell
(2024) among others.
The
route
(please click the link to see the route at the Ordnance Survey website):
Footpaths heading west from Chiddingstone Causeway, then southwest along a footpaths, will take us into Chiddingstone. Having admired the village, we will walk through the grounds of Chiddingstone Castle, crossing the lake and passing in front of the building. We will then head south along a lane to Hill Hoath, where we will join the Eden Valley Walk, a National Trail, before veering southeast towards another country lane. We will follow this in a southwesterly direction, before taking more footpaths to Smarts Hill, where we will stop for lunch at the pub. After lunch, we will walk around Smarts Hill and cross the B2188 to follow footpaths into Penshurst. We will then follow a footpath through Penshurst Park, affording good views of Penshurst Place. Emerging from the park at Cinder Hill, a short walk along a country lane, followed by a footpath, will take us to Moorden and then Station Hill, leading back to Penshurst Station.

Title: Bulcote and Burton Joyce short walk
Summary:
Join Alex for a slow walk in Nottinghamshire, with the potential for some autumn colour along the River Trent
Meeting at a railway station in rural Notts, this short walk has a bit of steep climb to begin with before falling back down to level with the River Trent. Along the way we will see the sights of two villages as well as getting some peaceful time along the slow flowing river.

Title: Codnor Park & Castle Circular
Summary:
Join Mark for a brilliant 14km (9-mile) circular walk through Derbyshire’s industrial history and picturesque countryside, perfectly timed before an evening of steam trains and fireworks just down the road!
Starting from the Codnor Park Reservoir car park, we will head out into the open countryside and make our way up to the 11th-century ruins of Codnor Castle—an excellent spot to pause and take in the views. From there, we will navigate a series of field boundaries and country trails before dropping down to pick up the Cromford Canal towpath.
The waterside return provides a relatively flat, well-surfaced stretch packed with local industrial heritage. As we trace the canal back through Golden Valley towards the reservoir, we will pass fantastic remnants of the area's past, including old lock workings, railway bridges, and the historic canal tunnels.

fireworks social event

Title: Bouldering MANCHESTER - Beginners welcome
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads For An Evening of INDOOR BOULDERING in Manchester!
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Bouldering is a form of climbing that focuses on shorter "problems" emphasising technique, balance, body positioning, and sometimes power, rather than long, high routes. Without the need for ropes, harnesses, and belaying, bouldering is an accessible activity for newcomers and is often considered the "purest" form of climbing.
Bouldering offers a wide range of benefits, including:
Physical:
Improved strength, tone, balance, power, and coordination.
Mental:
Enhanced problem-solving, focus, concentration, and body awareness.
Emotional:
Relaxation, a sense of achievement, and a feeling of mind-body connection.
Bouldering is also a fantastic way to meet new people and build lasting friendships, as it's an inherently social sport where climbers share tips and strategies to conquer the routes.
New to Bouldering?
If you're new to bouldering, it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader to learn the basics of safe bouldering. The leader can then introduce you to the rest of the group where you can refine your newly learnt skills in a social environment.
Experienced Boulderer?
If you’re new to climbing with ODL, the leader will help to introduce you to the rest of the group so you can explore the centre together.
You are responsible for your own safety and actions while bouldering. Please use your own judgement when accepting advice from OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers, regardless of your bouldering experience.
Ready to boulder?
You will need to sign up on the ODL event page. We would ask you to do this each time so that the leader has access to important information
If you are not already registered with Rock Over Climbing, please do so
here
to save time when you arrive. You only need to do this once.
When you arrive at the centre you will need to pay for entry and hire climbing shoes if you don't own a pair. ODL members benefit from the concessionary rate so please mention this when paying.
Get bouldering! You’ll find most of the group already bouldering so feel free to join them. If you’re new to bouldering with ODL, the leader will be looking out for you so if you spot them, please go speak with them first.
Any questions?
If you have any questions, please contact the leader directly.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by
Sieh
and joenellist.
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: Indoor Climbing MANCHESTER - Beginners welcome!
Summary:
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Join us for an evening of climbing in one of the UK's top climbing centres. Whether you are new to climbing or a seasoned climber, this centre offers something for everyone with a huge selection of routes including top rope, lead and auto belay.
Prefer to boulder? That's well catered for as well, with an extensive modern bouldering area ensuring there is plenty to keep you busy, or you can swap between climbing and bouldering on the same night.
Climbing is the main focus of the event, but this is also a great chance to meet other members and build lasting friendships. Many Outdoor Lads members join through climbing, so if you're new to the group and want to know more, come along and chat over a cuppa during the tea and cake break.
What to expect on your first climb with us?
If you are an experienced climber and have passed the centre's proficiency test, we'll pair you up with a climbing buddy and you'll be out exploring the centre in no time.
If you have never climbed before or think you could do with a refresher, we offer supervised climbing sessions with one of our leaders, subject to availability. That session will focus on introducing you to climbing, making sure you get plenty of time on the wall whilst also showing you how to belay safely. Due to the centre's rules, we are limited in the number of climbers the leader is able to supervise in each session so if you think you may need a supervised session,
please contact the leader before signing up to make sure there is enough space.
As a general guide, if you answer "no" to any of the following questions, you should opt for a supervised session:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie into a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay and lower down another climber correctly and confidently?
After a few supervised sessions, you should be ready to complete the centre's proficiency test and once that has been passed, you'll be able to climb with the rest of the group.
Everything else you need to know
You will need to register with Big Depot before your first visit to the centre but you only need to do this once. If you are an experienced climber, you can save time and do this online
here
, selecting the 18+ unsupervised option. This also applies if you just want to boulder, just select the relevant options during the registration. If you are a beginner and require a supervised session, the leader will help register you when you are at the centre.
Photos provided by Sieh and Dexmonster.
Difficulty & Distance: There is a range of routes of varying difficulty, but there should be something to suit everybody

Title: Channel Island Alderney Fort Clonque Experience
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for a once-in-a-lifetime experience, as we fly off across the Channel to spend
four Nights on the magical island of Alderney
. Lying only a few miles off the Normandy shore, Alderney is part of the Bailiwick of Guernsey in the Channel Islands.
About Alderney
With history and human remains dating back to the last major ice-age, Alderney has been an island for the better part of ten thousand years. Measuring only four square miles, with one parish (St Anne's), it is the third largest of the Channel Islands and the only remaining continental possessions of a Crown brought to us by William the Conqueror. The major fortifications were started by Henry VIII as part of his defence of the realm and were continued throughout the next four hundred years.
The position of the Channel Islands so close to France made them a perfect place for privateers, many of whom grew rich on their spoils. Indeed much of this loot was spent on some of the fine buildings still extant on the island. New forts, expanded church and warehouses and quays.
During the Victorian period, the British Government funded the building and upgrading of thirteen forts and naval installations. Among these included a new, much enlarged breakwater and Fort Clonque.
During the second World War, the British War Office and Winston Churchill decided that they were unable to defend the Channel Islands. Alderney, with a population of c.1500 was entirely evacuated in June 1940 leaving a deserted island which the German forces occupied. They quickly set about building parts of the Atlantic Wall, four internment camps and dozens of buildings. Due to blockading by the Royal Navy and the war crimes committed on the island, islanders were unable to return home until December 1945. When they did they found their houses ransacked, burnt down or simply destroyed.
For several years the island operated as a communal farm, with all profits going into a Government backed fund aimed at rebuilding Alderney. By 1948 Alderney had established a measure of self governance and were moved from the Home Office to the Baliwick of Guernsey for legal, economic and governance functions. This included the running of the airport and harbour facilities.
With these changes the island was able to move from an almost exclusively arable economy to a more service and tourism based system. Being part of the Baliwick had significant tax and business benefits and several large multinational enterprises base themselves in Alderney.
Between beautifully soft, sandy beaches and impressive cliffs, Alderney and its surrounding islets support a rich flora and fauna. Trees are rather scarce, as many were cut down in the 17th century to fuel the lighthouses on Alderney and the Casquets. Those trees that remain include cabbage trees, due to the mild climate – often miscalled "palms" but of the lily family), and there are some small woods dotted about the island. Puffins on Burhou and gannets on Les Étacs (popularly called Gannet Rock) just off Alderney are a great draw for many visitors to the island.
The Accommodation
We will be staying in the beautifully restored
Fort Clonque - a
Landmark Trust property - which has rather comfortable space for thirteen of us to stay. Perched on a rocky outcrop, the Fort is linked to the rest of the island by a tidal causeway.
Warm, cosy wood lined rooms, open fires and breath taking views are on offer at our accommodation. Rooms are mostly twin rooms, with private bathrooms. Living quarters are spread across several small buildings around the central courtyard. Take a look at the location, for my meagre description could never do this amazing place justice! No Smoking  and there is Little to No Internet at Fort Clonque.
Getting to Fort Clonque from Alderney Airport.
There is only one way to Fort Clonque, and this will be walking on the road from the airport to the fort, following a zigzag path down a cliff to Fort Clonque. I believe the distance is just 1-2 miles from the Airport to Fort Clonque.
Outline Itinery
Monday 17th May 2027 - Arrive at Fort Clonque from 1700 onwards. Tea, coffee  and evening meal will be provided. Time to relax or see what the night life is like on Alderney, please be aware of the tide times, as Fort Clonque will get cut off by the tides.
Tuesday 18th May 2027 - After continental breakfast of cereals, toast, jam, marmalade and tea and coffee Provided, there will be a walk around the island. There may be places on the island where we can stop off for lunch (at extra cost). During or after the walk there may be a pub stop before going back to the fort. This evening, we will venture out and try some of the local cuisine (extra cost).
Wednesday 19th May 2027 -
After the continental breakfast we will venture out around the island, there maybe an option of a island trip by boat (extra cost). Sightseeing around the area. We will find somewhere to stop for lunch. Head back to the Fort in the afternoon where you can relax before our evening meal in.
Thursday 20th May 2027 - After continental breakfast we will decide as a group what to do as this is the last full day on the Island. We will stop off somewhere for lunch. Tonight we will eat out at a restaurant as its the last night on the island.
Friday 21st May 2027  - After continental breakfast we will need to clean the fort before we leave to head home. We will need to leave the fort by 10am. There may be a little time to spend on the island depending on everyone's flight times.
Additional Costs
Flights and Ferries
As this event is on a island some forty minutes from mainland Britain, you will need to make your own way to the island of Alderney
Air Aurigny
Flies there from several mainland airports and is one option available to you. (Flight times with Aurigny are now available to book on their website.) Direct Flights to Alderney are only from Southampton Airport. Several UK Airports fly to Guernsey and change there for Alderney.
www.aurigny.com
Brittany Ferries
Depart Portsmouth for overnight sailing, Sunday 16th May 2027 departs at 1915 -  Arrives Guernsey at 0600 Monday 17th May 2027.Cabins are available on the Ferry.
Or depart Poole,
day time sailing to Guernsey. Departs Monday 17th May 1430, arrives Guernsey 1730
www.condorferries.co.uk
The price of the event includes - breakfast each day, tea and coffee, and dinner on two nights. We'll eat out on 2 nights, these nights you will need to pay for your own meals. You will need to buy your own drink - there are of course restrictions on the transport weights but there are shops in St Anne.
Payment by Instalments
OutdoorLads appreciates that not everyone may be able to pay for our events in one lump sum. If you would prefer to pay in instalments, please contact our office team at
support@outdoorlads.com
who will assist in setting up a payment plan to take payments in instalments.  Please note the final instalment will need to be made at least one month prior to the event to guarantee your place.

Title: Reading Social: Thai Me, Tease Me, Feed Me!
Summary:
Brighten up a dark and cold November Friday evening with a little spice! Join us for a Thai feast, good company and a chance to unleash your hidden beast. Come hungry… and bring your wild side! 😈
A Bit About The Venue:
ThaiGrr! is an independent Thai restaurant that pairs a traditional atmosphere with bold, uncompromising street food flavours. The restaurant has a contemporary interior inspired by the ancient, serene temples of Northern Thailand's Lanna Kingdom. The chefs craft regional dishes, ranging from comforting classics like Tom Yum soup to their signature, fiery Southern Thai minced pork dish known as "ThaiGrr’s Roar" (Kua Gling).
The restaurant closes at 9:30pm with last orders at 9pm, hence the 7pm start. For those who wish to stay out later we can move to a pub afterwards, for example The Alehouse in Broad Street, which is a popular haunt for those seeking a proper pub with real ale.
🐅 Why come along?
Unleash your hidden beast and spice up your November with an evening of Thai food, cheeky banter and great company! Whether you're new to OutdoorLads or a familiar face, come along, meet new people and catch up with friends. All you need to bring is yourself and a healthy appetite!

Spicy Thai food
to tantalise your taste buds
😈
A little heat, a lot of banter
and plenty of laughs
🍻
Friendly faces, old and new
in a relaxed setting
😂
Good food, great company
and stories worth sharing
📅
Find out what's coming up
with OutdoorLads locally and beyond

https://t.me/+EoB--tkEV3s4ZWJk

Title: Bonfire Night Special: Alton Towers Day Trip
Summary:
Join us for an unforgettable day of thrills, excitement and spectacular fireworks as OutdoorLads heads to
Alton Towers for the Ultimate Fireworks Night Spectacular!
🎆🎢
Alton Towers' spectacular end-of-season celebration combines world-class rollercoasters, dazzling lights and an epic fireworks display to bring the theme park season to a spectacular close. Whether you're a rollercoaster fanatic, a fireworks enthusiast or simply looking for a fun day out with great company, this is a brilliant opportunity to experience one of the park's biggest events of the year.
What to Expect
A full day exploring Alton Towers with a friendly group of OutdoorLads members
Thrilling rides and rollercoasters, including Nemesis Reborn, Wicker Man and The Smiler
The chance to experience some of your favourite rides after dark
Time to grab lunch, snacks and drinks together throughout the day
The highlight of the evening, Alton Towers' spectacular fireworks show, complete with music, special effects and an unforgettable finale
Whether you're there for the adrenaline rush, the spectacular evening entertainment or simply the chance to spend time with fellow members, there's plenty to look forward to!
Important Notes
🎟️
Tickets:
Tickets should be booked directly through the
Alton Towers website
in advance. We recommend booking early to secure your place and get the best available price.
🎢
Planning Your Day:

🎆
Evening Finish:

🗺️

If you're new to OutdoorLads, this is a great opportunity to meet fellow members, make new friends and enjoy a day out in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere. There's no pressure to ride every coaster or take part in everything. Come along, get involved at your own pace and enjoy the day with the group.

For Manchester’s Annual Festive December Social, Christmas Jumpers & Buffet!
Grab your Christmas jumpers, dust off those bobble hats and deck your balls… oops,
halls!
It’s time to get festive with OutdoorLads at our annual Manchester Christmas Social. Whether you’re rocking a classic Christmas knit, a flashing festive masterpiece or enough tinsel to decorate the entire North Pole, we want to see your best festive looks!
Join us at
Via on Canal Street from 7:30pm onwards
for a relaxed, informal evening bringing the OutdoorLads community together in the heart of Manchester’s Gay Village for drinks, conversation, festive fun and a little Christmas mischief.
🎄 What to Expect
Expect laughs, drinks, festive vibes and plenty of Christmas cheer throughout the evening. Christmas jumpers are highly encouraged, and the tackier, the better! Think flashing lights, inflatable reindeer, questionable Christmas fashion choices and full-on tinsel chaos.
And of course, what's Christmas without food?
Via Manchester and OutdoorLads
have kindly teamed up to provide a festive buffet of sandwiches, pizzas and finger foods, so there'll be plenty to tuck into while we celebrate the season together.
Whether you're a long-standing member or brand new to OutdoorLads, our socials are a great opportunity to catch up with old friends, meet like-minded people, swap stories from recent adventures and chat about upcoming events and trips. We pride ourselves on creating a warm, welcoming and inclusive space for everyone.
🎅 New to OutdoorLads?
If you're new to OutdoorLads, this is the perfect opportunity to come along, grab a drink, find a friendly face and get to know the group.
We know that walking into a room full of new people can sometimes feel daunting, so there's no pressure to know anyone beforehand. Our socials are relaxed, friendly and open to everyone, whether you're curious about joining, looking to make some new friends or simply fancy a festive night out.

Title: Of Mice and Men - Bingley Theatre
Summary:
Step out of the everyday and into an evening of compelling drama as we swap muddy boots for the theatre and settle in for a play that explores friendship, hope, loneliness and the pursuit of a better life.
Of Mice and Men
remains as powerful and thought-provoking today as ever.
Set during the Great Depression, the story follows George and Lennie, two travelling workers united by a simple dream: to own a small piece of land and build a better future for themselves. As they move from job to job, their friendship is tested by hardship, prejudice and circumstances beyond their control. When an opportunity arises in California, their dream finally seems within reach, but events take a tragic turn that leaves George facing an impossible decision.
Tickets are £17 (you'll need to purchase your own in advance), details are below. Seats are reserved, so we'll do our best to sit together.
Everyone is welcome on this relaxed evening. There’ll be chance to get to know one another and chat to other members. Whether you're new to OutdoorLads or been with us for a while, it'll be a friendly evening of fun. We'll meet for food before the event too - details will be shared closer to the time.

Title: Nottingham Bouldering (Lenton) - MONDAY - Beginners Welcome
Summary:
Swap trainers for climbing shoes and join OutdoorLads for an evening of INDOOR BOULDERING at Nottingham’s newest bouldering venue
NOTE: If you are climbing with us for the first time
, either as an experienced climber or beginner, please send a note to the
Event Leader
telling them about your experience and goals. There is a limit to the number of beginners that we can accommodate at each session. Each beginner needs to be supervised so we need to ensure there are enough experienced climbers to help you out. Climbing is great fun! It's a fab workout, in a social environment, and anyone can do it! Give it a go!
What is Bouldering?
It's a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes it an excellent activity for newcomers to the sport. No wonder it's often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
I'm new to Bouldering - can I come along?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
I've been Bouldering before?
As above, everyone attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you are responsible for your own safety, actions and involvement at all times. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.
To climb at Nottingham Climbing Centre you will need to:
-     Complete a climbing waiver for the centre (please arrive early to do this the first time, or better still complete it online before you arrive.) You can find the
link
to the waiver and bouldering safety video
here
on Nottingham Climbing Centre's website.
-     Pay the Lifetime Registration Fee - £6.00
-     Pay an Entry Fee directly to the climbing centre - £9.50 (ensure you mention ODL)
-     Hire shoes (if you don’t have your own) - £3.50*
*Equipment hire charges will be waived for your first visit to the centre!
If you have any questions or need any more information just get in touch with the event leader by clicking on their profile below, or take a look at the
My first climbing event page
for more information.
IMPORTANT!
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with some experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.

Title: NOTTINGHAM Indoor Climbing (Basford) – Beginners welcome
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads at Nottingham Climbing Centre
Climbing evenings are held regularly and we tend to go to the local pub – The Lion for refreshments and a social gathering afterwards where they have a wide variety of beverages both alcoholic and non-alcoholic.
NOTE: If you are climbing with us for the first time
, either as an experienced climber or beginner, please send a note to the
Event Leader
telling them about your experience and goals. There is a limit to the number of beginners that we can accommodate at each session. Each beginner needs to be supervised so we need to ensure there are enough experienced climbers to help you out. Climbing is great fun! It's a fab workout, in a social environment, and anyone can do it! Give it a go!
Nottingham Climbing Centre
Nottingham Climbing Centre is equipped with walls and routes to suit all skill levels and groups of climbers, whether you are a novice looking to try climbing for the first time, or an experienced lead climber, you’ll find an area to challenge you. With 28 Top Ropes routes available as well as 24 Lines of Lead climbing for the more advanced individuals. In addition, 6 auto-belays are available, so there is always the opportunity to climb, even if the numbers don’t match up. The available bouldering walls also provide that extra physical and mental challenge for those looking for something slightly different from rope work. Both Bouldering and Rope Climbing routes range from 4a – 8a.
I'm new to Climbing - can I come along?
If you've never climbed before or need a refresher, the leader will sign you into the climbing centre as a
supervised climber
so that you can come and give it a try (it can be helpful to message the leader to let them know). If you enjoy your climbing experience, and would like to come climbing more regularly, we will also happily show you the ropes and teach you everything you need to know to climb safely.
Do I need to be Supervised as a Climber?
If you answer
NO
to any of the following three questions, then you will need to arrange to be supervised. If you can answer YES to all these questions, you can sign up to this event as normal:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie yourself to the end of a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay another climber correctly and confidently?
To come along, you will need to register via this event page and to climb you will need to pay an entry fee directly to the climbing centre when you arrive, please see their
website
for up-to-date prices. We ask that all members sign up through the event page to make sure the event leader has all information of the members attending.
To climb at Nottingham Climbing Centre you will need to:
-     Complete a climbing waiver for the centre (please arrive early to do this the first time, or better still complete it online before you arrive)
-     Pay the Lifetime Registration Fee - £6.00
-     Pay an Entry Fee directly to the climbing centre - £9.50 (ensure you mention ODL)
-     Hire shoes (if you don’t have your own) - £3.50*
-     Hire a harness (again, if you don’t have your own) - £3.50*
-     Hire shoes and harness - £6.00*
*Equipment hire charges will be waived for your first visit to the centre!
Can I just come along and boulder?
Absolutely! Most of us do roped climbing, but if you prefer bouldering, you can sign yourself in and do it, as long as you can fill in the climbing centre's form correctly, watch their
safety video
and can answer the simple safety questions at reception on your first visit. Meet the group at the start; some others might be bouldering. We will make sure we come and find you when we have our tea break!
If you have any questions or need any more information just get in touch with the event leader by clicking on their profile below, or take a look at the
My first climbing event page
for more information.

Title: Hathersage, Stanage Edge & Padley Gorge Circular Hike
Summary:
Join Mark for a classic Peak District circular hike starting from Hathersage, taking in the dramatic gritstone escarpment of Stanage Edge and the ancient oak woodlands of Padley Gorge.
Starting from Hathersage, we head out along quiet tracks and field paths before climbing up to the iconic gritstone ridge of Stanage Edge. We will follow the cliff line with sweeping views across the Hope Valley, stopping at the famous
Robin Hood’s Cave
to explore and eat our packed lunch with a view.
From Stanage, we make our way south across moorland toward the Longshaw Estate, where we can pause at the
Longshaw Café
for a tea, coffee, or ice cream.
We will then descend through the ancient, tumbling streams and mossy oak woods of
Padley Gorge
, before following the valley footpaths and the River Derwent back into Hathersage for an optional post-walk pub drink.
Dogs:
Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but must be kept on a lead throughout the walk due to grazing livestock, wildlife, and ground-nesting birds on the moors.
New Members:
If this is your first event or you are new to OutdoorLads we’d love to see you. Please message me if you have any questions.
https://www.outdoorlads.com/my-first-event
Note:
If there are no places left on this event, join the waiting list, as people frequently drop out during the week before an event, and you are likely to get a place.
Image Credits:
All images taken by the walk leader.
Difficulty & Distance: Total distance is around 18km (11 miles) with 532m (1,750 feet) of ascent. Approximately 6 hours of walking. Some paths over fields are uneven and may be boggy in wet conditions.

Title: Greenfield to Newhey -GM9
Summary:
This is stage 9 of 20 on the Greater Manchester Ringway, a 200 mile (322km) walking trail exploring all 10 boroughs of Greater Manchester. You can find out more about it
here
.
This hilly stage of the trail explores the stunning landscapes of Saddleworth, the little bit of Pennine Yorkshire included within Greater Manchester.
Highlights include:
A rustic section of the Huddersfield Narrow Canal
The picture-postcard hilltop village of Dobcross
Aerial views of the Roman fort site at Castleshaw
A panoramic walk along the Standedge escarpment (part of the Pennine Way)
Crompton Moor and Crompton Fold country park, with its woodlands and waterfall.
Note that parts of the trail may be damp, muddy and slippery at any time of year and especially after periods of wet weather.
This is a linear walk
. See the options in the location details below.
Well-behaved, socialised and under-control dogs are welcome on this event.

Title: Friday walk: Red Deer & Edges Walk
Summary:
Join Ian on this fantastic walk on the Eastern Moors in the Dark Peak. Autumn is a magical time of the year where the trees start to change colour, bird song fills the air and the sound of the Red Stag bellowing to signal the start of the rut.
During Autumn as the light starts to fade and the days get shorter, Red Deer (largest mammal species) start to compete over the females, as they lock antlers they battle to win over their rival, the winner forming a harem (group of females or hinds).
This walk will start from Curbar Gap up along Curbar & Froggatt Edges with fantastic views over the Hope Valley. We’ll take in Longshaw Estate & Padley Gorge before our return leg over White Edge & Baslow Edge returning back to the carpark.
Please bring binoculars or scope for this walk, as you may get to see the Red Deer out on Big Moor which is a spectacle to see.
An optional refreshment in the Bridge Inn after the walk.

Title: Autumnal Amble Around The Piethorne Valley
Summary:
The South Pennines area has the greatest density of reservoirs in the country. There are six lying in and around the Piethorne Valley. The reservoirs were constructed to meet the demands of the surrounding mill towns and canal systems, producing scenes of calm beauty amid the rugged upland of the Pennines.
Our walk in glorious rolling Pennine countryside passes five of them, as we take a route in varied landscapes of moorland, farmland and woodland. We will then finish the walk at a nice pub close by.
Part of our route follows the Greater Manchester Ringway
https://www.gmringway.org/routes/stage-10-newhey-littleborough/

Title: Rewilding Visit @ Dundreggan
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads as we are invited to visit the Dundreggan Rewilding Centre in the Highlands of Scotland, the first visitor centre of its kind in the world.
Dundreggan, which is run by Trees for Life, is home to ancient pine woods, where we can experience rewilding in action, discover Gaelic culture and immerse ourselves in the wild beauty of the Scottish Highlands.
Our visit, free of charge, will include:
A talk by Stephen Couling, who works at Dundreggan and is an OutdoorLads member
Guide round the visitor centre
Tea / coffee and cake (that's got your attention), and
A chance to do one or more of the short walks at Dundreggan to see and feel at first hand what Rewilding is on the ground
Take a look at their own website to see more of the fantastic work they're doing to help rediversify our landscape, helping species to return in abundance.
Dundreggan welcomes dogs.
https://visitdundreggan.co.uk/

Title: 🍂 Autumn Activity Weeks - Into the Devil's Punch Bowl
Summary:
🍂 This event is part of our
Autumn Activity Weeks
— get active, get social and get out more!
The Devil's Punch Bowl is a vast 700-acre natural amphitheatre and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) east of Hindhead in the far south-west corner of Surrey. In the care of the National Trust since 1906, the Punch Bowl is a deep geological depression caused by spring water erosion of the mudstone layer under the sandstone surface.
This reasonably challenging 9-mile circular walk starting at Haslemere Station takes us up to the southern edge of the Bowl and then down through its wooded interior and back up again to the high point at Gibbet Hill, the second-highest point in Surrey at 892 feet (272m)
The sights:
Haslemere
: This town & civil parish of 17,000 people lies some 38 miles (62km) south-west of London close to the source of the River Wey (South). It does not appear in the Domesday Book, but rather seems to have originated in the late 12th century as a medieval 'planned town'. The London to Portsmouth railway reached Haslemere in 1859, sparking growth in the town, and it became a centre of the Arts & Crafts movement at the end of the 19th century.
The Devil's Punch Bow
l: This spectacular natural feature comprises a 300-foot deep, half-mile wide, depression in the land, surrounded by a rim rising to between 800 & 900 feet. All sorts of legends surround the origin of its name, which has been in use since at least 1768, and it has featured in the writings of Charles Dickens, C.S. Forrester and Agatha Christie among others. It became one of the National Trust's earliest acquisitions in 1906 and an SSSI in 1955 on account of its distinctive flora & fauna, including 60 breeding species of birds (see designation
here
).
The peace & quiet of the place was spoilt for many years by the main A3 London to Portsmouth road running around the rim of the Bowl, which in turn created a bottleneck on this major route. The problem was solved by the opening in July 2011 of a £371 million dual-carriageway tunnel under Gibbet Hill, since when the natural contours of the land have been restored.
The Sailor's Stone & Celtic Cross
: On 24th September 1786, an unknown sailor was murdered by three other sailors beside the old London to Portsmouth coaching road. The assailants were soon caught and hung on Gibbet Hill in April 1787. The Sailor's Stone was erected soon after the murder by the side of the road to commemorate the unfortunate victim. In 1851, a Celtic Cross was constructed on the site of the gibbet by a prominent judge in order to dispel the fears of local people.
Gibbet Hill
: At 892 feet (272m), this is the second-highest point in Surrey after Leith Hill, and commands panoramic views, especially to the north & east. On a clear day, prominent London landmarks such as Wembley Stadium may be seen. In the 18th century, the area had a poor reputation due to the activities of highwaymen and robbers.
During WWII and into the 1950's, Gibbet Hill was the site of an RAF ground radar navigational air station, consisting of four 240-feet masts sending pulses to aircraft to assist navigation (see link
here
). Tragically, on 6th May 1945, a USAAF aircraft flew into one of the poorly-lit masts in bad visibility and crashed on the hill with a total of 31 fatalities.
Temple of the Four Winds
: The stone base is all that survives of a fine hunting lodge constructed in 1910 by Viscount Pirrie, chairman of Titanic shipbuilders Harland & Wolff. With its magnificent views to the north, it was used for grand luncheon parties for Lord Pirrie's friends & guests. It fell into disrepair after WWII and was demolished in 1966, but the National Trust subsequently excavated & restored the foundations.
The route
(please click the link in
red
to see it):
From Haslemere station, we will leave the town via Weydown Road, Stoatley Hollow and Farnham Road to reach Hindhead Common and the National Trust visitor centre at the south-west corner of the Punch Bowl. After admiring the fine view from this point, we will descend steeply into the interior of the depression and walk north to Highcomb Farm and through Highcomb Bottom to reach the far point of the National Trust area at Vanhurst Copse. From here, we turn south and climb steadily up the eastern side of the Bowl, pausing at an open area near the top of the rim for a short lunch stop.
After the break, we complete the climb to reach the top of Gibbet Hill and the best views of the area.
We will then walk east through thick woodland to reach the Temple of the Four Winds, before turning south towards Haslemere, re-entering the town via Bunch Lane, Inval Hill, High Lane & Tanners Lane.
Dogs
Well-behaved dogs are welcome on this walk, and this is suitable for them, with few obstacles to negotiate. However, where we encounter grazing livestock or need to cross or walk along roads, dogs must be on a lead.
At all other times, a dog off the lead must be obedient.
Please note that only assistance dogs are allowed inside the National Trust café at the Visitor Centre.

Difficulty & Distance: Distance is 14.5 km (9 miles), total ascent is 440m (1,430 feet). Overall the route consists of two long climbs and descents, but within these there are a number of sharp gradients to tackle. Terrain is tarmac pavements & country paths & tracks.

Title: Ambergate to Duffield - DVH Way Section 6
Summary:
The Derwent Valley Trust
was set up in 1996 to promote the history, arts, wildlife and leisure opportunities that surround the river Derwent along its 55 mile course through Derbyshire.
The Derwent Valley Heritage Way
takes us from Ladybower Reservoir in the Peak District National Park to its end at Derwent Mouth where it flows into the River Trent near Shardlow.
The route is divided into eight sections of between  ~13 km (8 miles) and ~17 km (10.5 miles), each with a clear public transport solution. All, except the first section, are linear routes. We park at the end, travel to the start, and walk back to our cars. Sections 5, 6, 7 are brilliantly served by the East Midlands Railway Derwent Valley Line
(Derby–Matlock, hourly), which runs almost parallel to the trail the whole way. For sections (2, 3, 4 and 8), we use local buses.
Each section is a walk in itself. Join one or more, as you wish, or walk all eight sections to complete the whole route through Derbyshire. Please ask other attendees for a lift if you need one.
Section 6 – Ambergate to Duffield ~14 km (8.7 miles) Total ascent 228 m (748 ft)
This part of the route takes us to woods and fields from Ambergate before passing a large pond as it heads for Belper, a town that retains much of its intriguing industrial past. The town’s various mills loom into view as we approach Belper Bridge and the weirs. We pass the imposing East Mill and walk through the River Gardens before heading into the town centre.
Belper Park is a remnant of an old Royal forest. In the Middle Ages it was owned by the Duchy of Lancaster and used for breeding deer. From the park we head southwards to Milford where more factories were operated and powered by the Derwent.
At Makeney we will pause at the Holy Bush Inn for refreshments. From there we head across Duffield Bank, with fine views into the valley. At Duffield Bridge we make a short detour to visit to St Alkmunds Church before heading to the station.
Well behaved
dogs are welcome
but must kept under control at all times.

Title: The Calf & Cautley Spout: A Hike through the Howgills
Summary:
Join Outdoor Lads for an early spring mountain walk in The Howgill Fells. Being lesser known than the neighbouring Lake District and Yorkshire Dales, these fells are often quieter with a remote feel.
This is a walk of two halves, with the first section, starting in Sedbergh,  being on lower ground, following the Pennine Journey trail along the River Rawthey. However, the walk suddenly gains elevation as we walk up Cautley Spout and on to the top of the fells. We'll then follow the Dales High Way trail over the summits of The Calf (676m) and Calders (674m) before dropping back down to Sedbergh.
Points of interest on the route:
The Pennine Journey Trail:
This long distance walking trail is a recreation of one of Wainwright's journeys. The section we'll follow takes us along the River Rawthey, giving us great views up to some of the Yorkshire Dales' Fells and also through some protected woodlands where red squirrels live.
Cautley Spout:
This spectacular waterfall is England's highest and becomes increasingly more impressive as we approach along Cautley Holme Beck, with the cliffs of Yarlside to the East and Cautley Craggs to the West. This is also the toughest part of the walk, with the trail up the side of the falls being particularly steep. Though this steepness will give us plenty of excuses to pause and admire the falls.
The Calf
: The final ascent to the summit of The Calf is nice and gentle after the slog up the waterfall. Once on the summit we'll be greeted with one of England's most expansive views; being able to see the Lake District's peaks to the North West and Morcombe Bay to the South West. To the North East we'll see the Pennines highest peaks, with the hills of the Yorkshire Dales to the South East. We'll head south from here, enjoying great views of the rest of The Howgill Fells
Other Information:
Dog Suitability:
Dogs are always welcome on my walks, though their behaviour and safety is their owner's responsibility. This includes cleaning up after them, controlling their behaviour around other animals or people, and assisting them over any stiles or streams we may cross.
New Members

My First Event
page on the OutdoorLads website.

Title: Nottingham Bouldering (Lenton) - MONDAY - Beginners Welcome
Summary:
Swap trainers for climbing shoes and join OutdoorLads for an evening of INDOOR BOULDERING at Nottingham’s newest bouldering venue

Each beginner needs to be supervised so we need to ensure there are enough experienced climbers to help you out. Climbing is great fun! It's a fab workout, in a social environment, and anyone can do it! Give it a go!
What is Bouldering?
It's a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes it an excellent activity for newcomers to the sport. No wonder it's often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
I'm new to Bouldering - can I come along?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
I've been Bouldering before?
As above, everyone attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you are responsible for your own safety, actions and involvement at all times. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.

*Equipment hire charges will be waived for your first visit to the centre!

Title: Leeds Woodhouse Moor parkrun
Summary:
For those of you who enjoy your weekly parkrun fix, we'll be heading to the first ever parkrun out of London: Leeds Woodhouse Moor parkrun as part of our 'Christmas in Leeds' before the
Christmas in Leeds with Leeds Male Voice Choir Christmas Concert
and
Leeds Christmas Social
later the same day and
Knaresborough Christmas Markets
the next day. If you've not heard of it, parkrun is a free, weekly, timed 5k event that takes place every Saturday at locations across the world.
We will meet at 8.45am by the parkrun sign for a group photo. I'll be wearing a red parkrun t-shirt, and you're welcome to wear any OutdoorLads merchandise. You can register for parkrun and get your own barcode from
www.parkrun.org.uk
to scan at the end of your run to record your finish time if you wish. However, you do not need to do this to take part in the run if you don't want to.
Course description:
The course is 5k long, run on tarmac, gravel and trail paths. It's three laps and starts and finishes at the circular tarmacked area near Akmal’s Tandoori Bistro, just up from the A660 Woodhouse Lane.
It is run on tarmac paths, with a small section of flagstones which can be uneven and slippery. There are sections of the course prone to potholes and uneven surfaces, so we ask that you take care and watch your footfall during the event.
From the start, head towards the roundabout directly ahead, going anti-clockwise around it and exiting along the sixth path (last exit before completing a full circle). At the end of this path, take a sharp right around the outside of the Queen Victoria statue (over the flagstones) and follow the tarmac paths clockwise around the park, with a nice downhill towards the Robert Peel statue. Be wary of some uneven sections. At the corner by the skate park & Robert Peel statue, take a sharp right uphill, then the first left. Continue straight ahead, over the start area, towards the Queen Victoria statue and your second lap. At the end of the third (final) lap, bear right up the hill towards the start area to reach the finish.
On occasion parkruns can be cancelled due to the weather or lack of volunteers. Should this happen I will try to contact members as soon as I can.
