Title: Knaresborough Christmas Market - Circular walk from Bilton
Summary:
This is a circular 12.5K (8-mile) walk from the village of Bilton, through the Nidd Gorge and into Knaresborough. This is a relatively easy walk through beautiful broadleaf woodland. The route visits the Victorian Nidd Gorge Viaduct, 104 ft high, with seven arches and completed in 1848. It carried the North East Railway Line between Leeds and Thirsk and was closed in 1969. We will take some time to have lunch in Knaresborough and take in its
Christmas Markets
among a warren of medieval streets and stone staircases that weave their way up and down the hill. The town centre is perched on the cliffs above the River Nidd and the imposing railway viaduct. The walk returns through Conyngham Hall park, passing the Gardeners Arms pub, which you can stop at for a drink should you wish, though it will likely be getting dark by this point.

Please join the waiting list as people frequently drop out during the week before an event, and you are likely to get a place on the walk.

we’ll make sure you feel welcome. Please

, and don’t hesitate to drop me a message if you have questions or want to know more about this walk.

well-behaved dogs are welcome on the walk, but as we will be going through a busy Christmas market, this might not be suitable for your four-legged friend.

Title: Xmas Monday : Wellington Monument Post-Xmas Blowout
Summary:
Had your fill of dry turkey, endless tins of Quality Street, and slightly tense debates over Monopoly rules with the in-laws? Step away from the sofa!
This Christmas Monday Bank Holiday, lace up your boots and join us for a proper, invigorating winter circular across the Blackdown Hills National Landscape (AONB). It’s the ultimate antidote to Christmas overindulgence and seasonal family cabin fever—a chance to get out into the crisp winter air, blow away the festive cobwebs, and share some laughs with fellow OutdoorLads.
Event Overview
Date:
Monday 28th December 2026 (Christmas Monday Bank Holiday)
Start Time:
11:00 AM (aim for 10:45 AM to boot up)
Distance:
~8.5 miles (13.5 km)
Duration:
~4 to 4.5 hours
Difficulty:
Moderate. A classic rolling Blackdowns walk with some steady climbs up onto the commons and beacons, balanced by gentle descents and flat river valley paths.  Paths are likely to be very muddy.
The Route Highlights
Wellington Monument:
Starting high near this iconic 175-foot triangular obelisk, we’ll kick things off with sweeping views north across the Vale of Taunton Deane and over towards the Quantocks.
Black Down Common & Sampford Point:
Crisp, open walking across rugged heathland tracks with expansive vistas across the Devon and Somerset borders.
Culmstock Beacon:
Heading out to the historic beacon site perched high on the ridge, offering spectacular panoramic vistas over the Culm Valley.
The Culm Valley & Hamlets:
Dropping off the high ground, we’ll meander through quiet rural lanes and winter bridleways passing Dalwood, Whitehall, and Tedburrow.
Hemyock & The Climb Back:
Passing just north of historic Hemyock and Castle Hill before following the sheltered tracks up Pen Cross and Whitehall to complete our circuit back at the Monument.
Dogs
Dogs are welcome to join us on this event but we do ask the following:
Please appreciate the fact that not everyone is a dog owner or lover- especially when we stop to eat
Please ensure you adhere to the Countryside Code at all times - see (
Keeping Dogs Under Effective Control)
If your dog is uncontrolled and strays in open land frightening other animals or livestock, the leader is supported by the OutdoorLads board of trustees to ask you to leave the event as this is not acceptable behaviour.

Title: Outdoor First Aid Course for Leaders - Stockport
Summary:
This training course is funded by OutdoorLads for leaders, especially Mountain Walk Leaders, Outdoor/Sport Climbing Leaders, and Mountain Biking Leaders.
These leaders are required by our insurance policy to have had Outdoor First Aid training to lead these event types. Other outdoor event leaders, including lowland and hill leaders may book on to this course, but those required to complete the training will be prioritised should a waitlist develop.
This 16-hour outdoor first aid course deals with issues involved with the long term care of casualties in a remote setting. It is often referred to as a wilderness first aid or a remote first aid.
The outdoor first aid course includes primary and secondary surveys of a casualty, we also look at first aid equipment and how you may adapt and improvise your own equipment to support your first aid kit.
A lot more emphasis is placed on incident management and relaying information to rescue teams in the outdoors. We assume minimal outdoor equipment is available and there are plenty of opportunities to practice first aid.
This 2 day (16 hour) course is recognised by the National Governing Bodies such as the Mountain Leader Training, British Canoe Union, British Cycling, British Association of Snowsport Instructors etc.
Event cost
To help us ensure that those that book on to this event are committed to it, we're asking Leaders to pay £15. This payment will be refunded in full once attendance on the course is confirmed after the event. If you cancel before the event and we can fill your place, you will be refunded in full, but otherwise your booking on this event is subject to the
OutdoorLads refund policy
.
OutdoorLads will subsidise your course fee, you are responsible for your own travel, food and accommodation costs. The course lasts for two days, starting early each morning and finishing in the evening each day and you are required to attend both days.
Please note that places on this are for leaders, and those who have already applied to become leaders. If you have any doubts, please contact the OutdoorLads office to discuss.

Title: Christmas in Brixham 2026
Summary:
Brixham offers a truly unique setting, combining the charm of a traditional fishing town with the dramatic beauty of the South Devon coastline. During the festive season, the harbour comes alive with sparkling lights, seasonal decorations and a warm community atmosphere that creates an unforgettable backdrop, whether it's coastal walks along the South West Coast Path, or festive wondering through the town, Brixham provides a refreshing alternative to the typical Christmas venue.
The Accommodation
Our venue is an Outdoor Education Centre located right in the harbour and provides a large lounge area and separate dinning room, and with a bit of OutdoorLads festive magic, we'll soon have it looking like Santa's Grotto!   You can expect dormitory style bedrooms of various sizes with plenty of spare beds to allow us to spread out.
Itinerary
The following is all subject to change but should give you and idea of what to expect if this is your first OutdoorLads Christmas event.
Friday
You'll be able to arrive at the site from around 5pm on the Friday, and find the bed you've reserved (more details on this closer to the time). Once settled in, there is plenty of room to relax in the lounge, with hot drinks available throughout the weekend. If your preference is for an alcoholic tipple you'll need to bring these yourself.
Friday evening will be jacket potatoes with a choice of fillings, but we're not completely forgetting the traditional OutdoorLads buffet. We'd like you to bring along something for desert or an offering for a cheese board to be set out on both evenings.
Once we've had a briefing over the plans for the weekend, we'll be looking for some volunteers to tidy up the kitchen and dining room, whilst the others can head back to relax in the lounge, or perhaps enjoy some board games (don't forget to bring your favourites).
Saturday
After breakfast on Saturday morning you'll head out on your choice of activity , returning to our accommodation early afternoon. This means you will likely need a packed lunch that you will need to bring yourself.
For those of you that like your ParkRun on a Saturday morning, the nearest is Torbay and if there is sufficient demand we'll try to arrange drivers for those that need it and time our daytime activities to give you a chance to do both.
OutdoorLads hostel events always rely on everyone mucking in and helping in the kitchen over the weekend and Christmas is no different, so whilst a few volunteers are busy in the kitchen, we'll hopefully have some Christmas themed activities in the lounge including our traditional Secret Santa.
It wouldn't be a Christmas hostel without Christmas dinner. and you can expect a starter, traditional Christmas roast, vegan option and all the trimmings followed by dessert.
We'll need some volunteers to clear up in the kitchen and dining room, but once that's done it will be a chance to relax and digest, there could be some music on but I'm sure the board games will be in full swing again.
Sunday
Start the day with breakfast and as much coffee as needed to recover from the night before, and then we'll spend an hour or so tidying up the venue and leaving it as clean, or even cleaner than we found it.
Our plan is to offer a short walk or cultural event on the Sunday for those that are not in a hurry to leave, but this is subject to volunteers stepping up to lead this for you!

Title: Family Christmas in the Yorkshire Dales
Summary:
A Christmas of memories with your OutdoorLads family.
We wish you a Family Christmas, we wish you a Family Christmas…
so come spend it with us in the Yorkshire Dales.
Family Christmas returns to Yorkshire, in one of the most welcoming spots we know! Join Chris and Mike for a festive three-nights in the Yorkshire Dales.
Whether you’re looking for a change from your usual plans or simply want somewhere to belong this year, we’ll be here to cook for you, laugh with you, and keep the festive spirit flowing. Accommodation
Our venue is a spacious independent hostel with a good size lounge and separate dining room, cosy conservatory area and a large kitchen together with bike store and a range of bedroom sizes. Outside, there's a large garden with beautiful views in every direction. If the weather is good there's a firepit, and a chance to relax around a fire. If not don't worry, we have the cosy hostel for comfort, relaxing chatting, board games etc.
There is no TV and while there is WiFi it can be patchy, so this hostel is a chance to socialise away from our screens!
There's a small but well stocked village shop a short walk away and provides all you may need, and there's a choice of excellent pubs in the village serving home cooked food (depending upon their Christmas opening times).

Title: Hogmanay / Oidhche na Bliadhn 2026
Summary:
Join us for FOUR nights as we see in the new year in typical Scottish style.
This years venue is the ferry port of Oban, easily reached by road and rail so there's no excuse that it's too far away.
The area of Oban and it's surrounds will surprise you - it's not just a ferry port...  There is a good number of easy to moderate walking options in the local area; the islands of Mull, Lismore & Kerrera are reached from Oban by ferry and all have walking and history to explore; the mountains of Argyll are a short drive away; and for those wanting to know more of the history of Scotland, Kilmartin Glen is to the south - where you can find Dunadd, believed to be the capital of the ancient kingdom of Dal Riata which was a precursor to the Scottish kingdom.
As is the Scottish tradition we will be getting glammed up to see in the New Year (kilts are optional).
As in years past we are having had a themed evening, this year's theme being kids film and TV characters - will we see the Teletubbies, Zippy, George and Bungle or the Family Ness appear?
Dogs:

Title: Sheffield Bouldering @ The Climbing Hanger
Summary:
Swap trainers for climbing shoes and join OutdoorLads for an evening of INDOOR BOULDERING at The Climbing Hanger in Sheffield.
Cards/contactless ONLY  - this venue does not accept cash
If you haven't been to The Hangar before, please click
here
to pre-register. Click on the link, scroll down, select Sheffield and follow the on-screen instructions. Completing the waiver prior to arrival will get you climbing faster.
What is Bouldering?
It's a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes it an excellent activity for newcomers to the sport. No wonder it's often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
I'm new to Bouldering - can I come along?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
I've been Bouldering before?
As above, everyone attending the event  must abide by the centre's T&Cs etc. As an experienced boulderer you responsible for your own safety, actions and involvement at all times. As such, you should use your own judgement in taking up advice given either by OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by the event leader / venue.
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with some experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: OutdoorLads x CatZero: A Norwegian Epic
Summary:
OutdoorLads are setting sail across the North Sea once again - this time on a one-way voyage to Norway!
Following our fantastic past adventures with CatZero, we’re delighted to offer this incredible 8-day expedition. You don’t need any past sailing experience to join! Whether you're an absolute beginner who has never set foot on a boat or a qualified sailor, these trips are open to everyone. You’ll learn everything you need to know to sail the ship under the expert guidance and direction of the fantastic CatZero team.
CatZero is a 72-foot Challenge Round the World Racing Yacht with a "Category Zero" rating, meaning she can sail anywhere in the world in all conditions. CatZero is also the name of the charity that owns and operates the vessel.
This is not a leisure holiday! Voyages aboard CatZero are interactive, hands-on, fun, utterly exhausting, and deeply rewarding. You’ll be living in close proximity with the rest of the team and working together throughout the trip.
While making our 450-nautical-mile passage across the North Sea, we will split into two watches, alternating every four to six hours to rest and work, including through the night. Everyone takes an active role in running the boat: from cooking, cleaning, and scrubbing the decks, to handling sails and steering. Teamwork and camaraderie will be in abundance, and while you’ll be exhausted by the end, you’ll have had the absolute time of your life, have learned a lot about sailing, yourself, and your crew-mates, and created memories to last a lifetime.
Included as part of this trip, you can even complete the RYA Competent Crew qualification!
💬 Past feedback 💬
"The whole event was simply awesome. The crew were fantastic headed by Nick who led the voyage with humour and excellent instruction assisted by lizzy the first mate, Mike and gracie the volunteers I am unable pull any negatives only positives, from the way all participants came together, working and living in such close proximity. The food was enjoyable and sustaining. But the absolute highlight was the team work and instruction we had enabling us to sail a sail boat across the north Sea where we had some of every weather type and saw a few struggling with their sea legs but what an experience. As a new member I cannot thank Dan for organising, Nick for skippering and every participant including the above for their friendship and commeraderie. I really cannot wait for the next trip with cat zero thank you xxx"
"I absolutely loved every single minute of this trip from start to finish – it was truly unforgettable. The staff and volunteers pitched everything perfectly, striking just the right balance, and it was such a privilege to be able to take part. This has easily been my favourite OutdoorLads event to date. Please give us more opportunities like this – I’d jump at the chance to do it again, and I’d love to go to Norway next time!"
"...All the crew were absolutely amazing. A special shout out to Simon and Gracey who kept us going through tough shifts with great humour and excellent teaching. I left the boat feeling relaxed, accomplished and a huge grin on my face. Definitely my favourite ODL event so far."
Rough Itinerary
Friday 4th June:
Join the boat at 17:00 in Hull for introductions, kitting up, and boat familiarisation in preparation for the voyage ahead. We'll spend our first night aboard the vessel in Hull.
Saturday 5th June:
Bright and early at 07:00, we depart Hull and set off on our 450-nautical-mile journey across the North Sea toward Norway.
Exploring Norway & Lysefjord:
Upon arrival in Norway, we'll have the chance to visit the vibrant city of Stavanger before heading out to explore the surrounding beautiful islands and breathtaking fjords. Weather and conditions permitting, we hope to stop down the dramatic Lysefjord for a hike up to Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock), standing 604 metres high, to take in the awe-inspiring views down the fjord.
Saturday 12th June:
The voyage concludes in Stavanger. Departure from the yacht is by 16:00, with flexible timing to accommodate flight times and onward travel.
If you need travel inspiration for the return journey, I'll list my plans in the Location section at the bottom of this event page once planned.

CatZero or OutdoorLads will take no responsibility for loss or damage of personal belongings on this event, and will accept no liability.
CatZero or OutdoorLads have no liability to the participant in the event the participant fails to board the yacht prior to sailing, unless caused by the negligence of CatZero or its representatives.
Health
You must be mentally and physically fit for the sail. All participants must be in general good health.
You will be required to complete a medical questionnaire prior to sailing, and you must make CatZero aware of any injuries, illnesses and/or medications you are taking. You must notify CatZero of any changes between comlpetion of the medical questionnaire and the sailing.
CatZero can refuse to accept you if they believe that the safety and/or smooth running of the sail would be at risk due to any injuries or illness a participant has, or due to any other medical reason.
Safety
The safety of all participants is of paramount importance to CatZero. Sailing can be dangerous and hazardous, and all participants must accept those risks and always have regard to the safety of themselves and third parties.
Whilst on the yacht, all participants must comply at all times with the authority, decisions, and instructions of the Skipper. All participants must comply with with all safety guidelines and instructions given by the Skipper and other CatZero representatives.
All participants must not engage in any activity, whether shore based or on board the yacht, which is likely to compromise their safety or the safety of any other person.
Failure to comply may result in the Skipper ask the individual to vacate the yacht.
The Skipper or CatZero will have the absolute authority, without providing any prior notice, ask an individual or individuals to vacate the yacht if the safety or smooth running of the sail is deemed to be at risk.
In the event that an individual is asked to vacate the yacht, CatZero will not be liable for costs incurred.
Insurance
CatZero or OutdoorLads do not provide any insurance covering the participant.
The participant is responsible for making their own arrangements for adequate insurance to cover the cost of personal accident, personal liability, medical expenses, and emergency repatriation during the sail, including travel to/from the yacht.
The participant agrees to indemnify CatZero in respect of any costs or expenses claimed against CatZero or incurred by CatZero which would ordinarily be covered by adequate insurance taken out by the participant.
Behaviour
Throughout the period of the sail, both when ashore and on board the yacht, all participants shall:
behave in a moderate and reasonable manner, taking into account of the people around them
do nothing which may render the yacht liable to arrest or impounding
not take or consume personal stocks of alcohol on board the yacht
not behave in a manner that is or is likely to be disruptive, abusive, antisocial, dangerous, or likely to cause upset or distress to any third party or damage to property
Not use, carry, or store any illegal drugs, substances or any other illegal items
Not engage in any activity which is likely to compromise the reputation of CatZero
If in the Skipper's reasonable opinion, any participant is in breach of the above, in any way, they shall have the absolute authority, without providing prior notice, to ask them to vacate the yacht.

Title: Audley End Stately Home Visit & nearby Market Town Explore
Summary:
Start the New Year with a lovely day out combining the grand architecture of 17th Century built Audley End Stately Home and it's impressive gardens and grounds
*
. There will also be some short landscape walking, exploring the nearby historic market town with of course a pub break. All within an hour by train from London.
*
Cost for entry to the house and gardens are £20.06 in advance online or £23.60 on the day. Both minus £1.50 for concessions. (prices as of Sept 26) The estate is English Heritage run so if you are an existing member of this then your entry will be free of charge (just remember your card!)  See further below for link to the Historic England website for more images, info and booking details.
Itinerary
We will head out from our start point on a scenic 1.5-mile easy walk toward the estate, passing through the some pretty North Essex countryside.
Upon arrival at Audley End House itself, we will have 3.5 to 4 hours hours to explore this incredible English Heritage site.
* Explore inside : Check out the grand Jacobean Great Hall, The State Rooms and Intimate Private Apartments, all decorated with fine furniture and works of art & the libraries packed with historic red-and-gold leather books.
* Explore Below Stairs: Walk through the Victorian Service Wing to see where the famous 19th-century cook Mrs Avis Crocombe worked.
* The Grounds: Wander the impressive gardens and parkland designed by ‘Capability’ Brown, visit the resident horses in the stable block, and see the organic kitchen garden.
* Lunch: You can either grab a quick lunch/coffee at the cafe or tea room; or eat packed lunches in the grounds
Next, we take a gentle 1-mile walk from the house into the historic centre of Saffron Walden for a scenic circular walk taking in:
* St Mary’s Church (the largest parish church in Essex)
* The flint ruins of the 12th-century Walden Castle
* Bridge End Garden (featuring a beautifully restored Victorian hedge maze)
* The historic Market Square with working market on a Saturday.
Then it'll be time for the essential liquid refreshment stop at a gorgeous historic 16th-century half-timbered pub.
Finally - because it'll be dark by the time we leave the pub, we'll avoid walking the 2 miles back to the event start by catching the bus for a ten minute ride back.
Link to English Heritage - Audley End House for more info and booking etc
https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/places/audley-end-house-and-gardens/
Is it dog friendly?
Dogs are allowed in the grounds of Audley End House but not within the house itself (except for assistance dogs).
New Members
- We would like to warmly welcome any newbies looking perhaps to try this as their first Outdoor Lads event. You may find this link useful
https://www.outdoorlads.com/my-first-event
or if you have If you have any questions then feel free to message either of us.
Want to Get Out More?
To be informed of all our East Anglia events please click on this Telegram link
https://t.me/joinchat/AAAAAFQJUXCw99c0mOHLiQ
Photo Credits:
All photos taken by OutdoorLads Members and permission is granted to OutdoorLads for further use.
Difficulty & Distance: There is a walking total (excluding around the house and estate itself) of approx 2.5 miles.  Fairly flat and along hard paths or tarmac.

Title: Edinburgh Spooky Social
Summary:
Edinburgh becomes a different city at the end of October. The nights draw in early, the closes feel colder, and the Old Town seems to breathe a little heavier. Join us on Friday 30th October for a short, atmospheric OutdoorLads evening walk through some of Edinburgh’s hidden lanes, eerie gateways, and genuinely haunted corners — finishing with a warm, sociable meal at China Red Buffet.
This isn’t a tourist ghost tour. It’s a relaxed wander through places with real stories: forgotten graveyard paths where poltergeists have scratched visitors, narrow closes once used by body‑snatchers, stone steps echoing with the final footsteps of the condemned, and back lanes where Burke & Hare hunted their last victim. All true, all tucked away from the crowds, and all perfect for the night before Halloween.
We’ll begin at the quieter entrance to Greyfriars Kirkyard, exploring its lesser‑known corners and hearing a few of the darker tales connected to the graves. From there, we slip down the hidden closes of Candlemaker Row, pass under the shadowy arch of Potterrow Port, climb the dramatic steps of The Vennel, and weave through the West Port back lanes before finishing at China Red Buffet for food, warmth, and a relaxed social evening.
The walk is only 2 km, taken at an easy pace with plenty of stops for stories, photos, and chat. It’s ideal for new members, regulars, and anyone who enjoys Edinburgh’s atmospheric side — especially at this time of year.
Expect atmosphere. Expect laughs. Expect a few goosebumps. And expect a great night out with the lads.

Title: Bouldering MANCHESTER - Beginners welcome
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads For An Evening of INDOOR BOULDERING in Manchester!
This event is intended as a safe space for the LGBTQ+ community; everyone will be warmly welcomed
Bouldering is a form of climbing that focuses on shorter "problems" emphasising technique, balance, body positioning, and sometimes power, rather than long, high routes. Without the need for ropes, harnesses, and belaying, bouldering is an accessible activity for newcomers and is often considered the "purest" form of climbing.
Bouldering offers a wide range of benefits, including:
Physical:
Improved strength, tone, balance, power, and coordination.
Mental:
Enhanced problem-solving, focus, concentration, and body awareness.
Emotional:
Relaxation, a sense of achievement, and a feeling of mind-body connection.
Bouldering is also a fantastic way to meet new people and build lasting friendships, as it's an inherently social sport where climbers share tips and strategies to conquer the routes.
New to Bouldering?
If you're new to bouldering, it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader to learn the basics of safe bouldering. The leader can then introduce you to the rest of the group where you can refine your newly learnt skills in a social environment.
Experienced Boulderer?
If you’re new to climbing with ODL, the leader will help to introduce you to the rest of the group so you can explore the centre together.
You are responsible for your own safety and actions while bouldering. Please use your own judgement when accepting advice from OutdoorLads Volunteers or other experienced climbers, regardless of your bouldering experience.
Ready to boulder?
You will need to sign up on the ODL event page. We would ask you to do this each time so that the leader has access to important information
If you are not already registered with Rock Over Climbing, please do so
here
to save time when you arrive. You only need to do this once.
When you arrive at the centre you will need to pay for entry and hire climbing shoes if you don't own a pair. ODL members benefit from the concessionary rate so please mention this when paying.
Get bouldering! You’ll find most of the group already bouldering so feel free to join them. If you’re new to bouldering with ODL, the leader will be looking out for you so if you spot them, please go speak with them first.
Any questions?
If you have any questions, please contact the leader directly.
Photos : Copyright granted to OutdoorLads by
Sieh
and joenellist.
Difficulty & Distance: Suitable for all abilities. If you're new to bouldering, just let the event leader know and we'll get you started!

Title: Coombes Valley and the Staffordshire Moorlands
Summary:
Join us for a walk through the Coombes Valley RSPB Reserve and the Staffordshire moorlands, south of Leek.
This is a circular walk of 9 miles / 14.5 kilometres, with around 300 metres of ascent.  We’ll be walking through woodlands and across open grassland, along farm tracks and quiet country lanes.
The Coombes valley is steep-sided and the Coombes brook, a tributary of the river Churnet, flows through it. The valley is densely wooded, with a mix of beech, oak and silver birch trees.  This provides ideal cover for woodland birds. In spring and early summer, migrating
Flycatchers
, and
Redstarts
come to breed. Redwings,
Fieldfares
and Finches are regular visitors in winter.  We may hear a
Woodpecker
and we’ll certainly see some
Pheasants
.  The valley is also one of a few locations where you may find the scarce
Argent and Sable Moth
.
If you have a head for heights and can cope with wooden slats and a rope bridge, you can experience the woodland canopy walkway which projects from the steep side of the valley!
Around the valley, the countryside is fairly open and feels remote.  We’ll pass by Sharpcliffe Hall, a lovely old stone country house dating back to 1673.  Crossing Ferney Hill (285 metres), towards the end of the walk, we’ll have some good views of the Roaches and the Churnet valley across the rolling Staffordshire moorlands.
Note
: parking at the start of this walk is limited, so we’ll meet up in the nearby town of Leek and then drive the short distance to the start point in as few cars as possible.  See ‘Location’ for further information.
Dogs

please do not bring your dog on this walk
as the RSPB does not permit dogs in the reserve, in order to protect sensitive wildlife.

Title: Lanty's Tarn, Grisedale and Ullswater hike
Summary:
Join Steven for a moderate walk exploring the area around Glenridding and Patterdale in the northeast corner of the Lake District National Park.
This is an undulating route that is all about the mountain and lake views with a small section being part of Alfred Wainwright's Coast to Coast Walk.
The walk is around three valleys and a brief part is closer to the lakeshore and is a really good introduction to the area without any significant elevation been reached.
Setting off for the only climb of note the chosen gradual ascent crosses over the lower part of the mountain ridge of Birkhouse Moor to a nice picture postcard spot by a tarn before descending into Grisedale for the spectacular view of the high peaks and crag scenery towards the head of the valley.
Joining Wainwright's path to descend gradually towards the village of Patterdale we continue to cross over the river to meet a bridleway on the slopes of Place Fell this then takes us to the col between Silver Crag and Place fell.
The descent in between Juniper trees is very pleasant and we will then turn back on a lower bridleway above the lake to return to the start around the head of the lake at a lower level.
So please come along and celebrate the weekend of Halloween with this less challenging but highly rewarding wander.
This route is suitable for well behaved dogs but will involve a couple of ladder stiles in the early part of the walk. Please keep dogs on leads when in areas with livestock.
Photo / Image Credits
: All images here were taken by the leader Steven and permission is granted for use in this page and any future OutdoorLads pages
Difficulty & Distance: 17km/10.5miles two moderate climbs, rough rocky paths and bridleways

Title: Manchester’s Halloween Social! Spooky Spectacular
Summary:
Another year without BIG Halloween - we know, we’re disappointed too! But that doesn’t mean spooky season is cancelled. Join us for OutdoorLads’ Manchester Halloween Social where we’ll be bringing the OutdoorLads community together in the heart of Manchester’s Gay Village for a relaxed, informal evening of drinks, conversation, connection and a healthy dose of Halloween mischief. We’ll be meeting in the downstairs area of Via on Canal Street, starting from 7pm.
🎃 What to Expect
Expect laughs, drinks, spooky vibes and plenty of Halloween fun throughout the evening. Costumes are highly encouraged - the gayer and ghoulier, the better! Whether you arrive as a terrifying creature of the night, a camp Halloween icon, or simply yourself, you’ll be very welcome.
Whether you are a long-standing member or brand new to OutdoorLads, our socials provide the perfect environment to meet like-minded people, share stories from recent adventures, catch up with old friends, and chat about upcoming events and trips. We pride ourselves on being a warm, inclusive space for everyone.
👻 New to OutdoorLads?
If you are new to OutdoorLads, this is the perfect opportunity to drop by, grab a drink, find a friendly face and introduce yourself to the group. We understand that taking the first step into a new social circle can sometimes feel daunting - if you have any concerns regarding fitness, ability, or simply aren't sure if OutdoorLads is the right fit for you, please come along for a casual drink.
It’s a great opportunity to meet members in a relaxed setting, make some new friends and experience the welcoming culture of our community without needing to commit to a hike or other outdoor activity.
🧛 Got Questions?

We’ll be meeting in the downstairs area of Via on Canal Street from 7pm. So grab your costume, summon your courage and come join us for a suitably spooky OutdoorLads evening in Manchester!

Getting Here:
Via is centrally located in Manchester’s Gay Village on Canal Street and is easily accessible by public transport. The venue is just a short walk from Manchester Piccadilly and Manchester Oxford Road train stations. The area is also well-served by local Metrolink tram stops and numerous city centre bus routes. For those planning to drive, there are plenty of car parks available within walking distance of Canal Street. We recommend using the Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) website or app to check the latest travel updates for your journey.
Staying Overnight:
If you are travelling from further afield and looking to stay the night, Manchester city centre offers a wide range of accommodation to suit all budgets. There are many hotels within a 5–10 minute walk of the venue, including options around Piccadilly Station and St Peter’s Square. We recommend booking in advance, particularly around Halloween and during busy weekends or local events.

Title: Caernarfon Coastal New Year Walk
Summary:
This 6 mile circular walk starts off from near the quayside - where thousands of tons of slate were exported during the 19th century.
We will cross the river on the swing bridge and go to a viewpoint over the town, where the mountains of Eryri form an impressive backdrop.
We'll then take the Wales coast path (a minor road at this point) which has lovely views of the Menai Straits for a couple of miles.
After that we will head inland passing an ancient church and crossing a small hill with further views, and through some farms to pick up the course of the Welsh Highland steam railway.
If the garden centre here is open we can get tea and cake. A level footpath follows the rail line back into the town.
Caernarfon is a walled  town with nearby Roman origins, however the castle and walls were built in the 13C by the English King Edward 1st.
It is now a designated World Heritage Site and the imposing castle is one of the largest in Wales. Dolphins are often seen just offshore. The little streets within the town walls are picturesque and fascinating to explore.

Please fill in the online registration form for the Climbing District centres we use for this event. This will save time on your first initial admission to the centre(s).
https://climbingdistrict.uk/first-time-at-climbing-district/
Bouldering is a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems', as they are referred to, tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes the activities excellent for newcomers to the sport.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
Do I need a guided session?
If you have never tried bouldering before it is recommended that you have a guided session from the event leader, who will go through everything you will need to know to boulder safely before joining in with the rest of the group.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre’s staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.
Independent boulderer?

Title: Winter Ware and Cold Christmas
Summary:
Join Alex for this ten-mile winter walk from Ware to Cold Christmas via Yuletide Youngsbury.
We will meet outside Ware station and head north and uphill through the town towards the fields that lie beyond. We will cross undulating countryside as we head towards the ruined Thundridge Old Church, dating from the 15th century but replaced in the 1850s. Only the tower and the graveyard remain, and it is believed to be one of the most haunted churches in the country.
From here we will turn west and head through the villages of Thundridge and Wadesmill, which lie on the Roman road Ermine Street. After crossing the River Rib, we will veer northwest and enter Youngsbury Estate. The gardens were landscaped by Capability Brown and we will ascend gently through them towards the main house, which was built in 1745. Our route will skirt the perimeter of the estate, turning south past the timber buildings of Home Farm.
We will continue south via the Harcamlow Way towards the tiny but aptly named settlement of Cold Christmas. Our route will initially head uphill onto the plateau between the Rivers Rib and Ash, before gradually descending into the Ash Valley, with views of the surrounding hills, woodland and farmland. We will then turn southwest and trace the course of the river through the Amwell Nature Reserve where it flows into a system of lakes.
Finally we will meet the River Lee (or Lea), now more of a canal after centuries of human influence, and we will follow its banks for the final part of our route, which will take us back into Ware. From here it is a short walk to the station or to one of its riverside pubs.

Title: BIRMINGHAM Indoor Climbing - MONDAY - Experienced
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for an evening at Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre.
"EXPERIENCED" in this instance is those that have previously climbed & can answer YES to all three of these questions:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie in to a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay another climber correctly & confidently?
Please ensure you only sign up for this event if you
satisfy all three of the prerequisites as an experienced (independent) climber!
Never climbed before? Need a refresher on the basics? Answered NO to any of the three questions above? You will need to
attend one of the beginners (supervised) events
instead, where we will happily sign you in to be supervised (two people per leader maximum), show you the ropes & teach you everything you need to know to climb safely! Beginner (supervised) events are not offered every week.
If you are climbing with us for the first time, whether Experienced or Beginner, it is essential that you send a note to the Event Leader telling them about your previous climbing experience & your goals!
Bouldering
- Most of us do roped climbing, but if you prefer to do bouldering, you can sign yourself in & go bouldering (unsupervised) instead of, or as well as, roped climbing. Please meet the leader & the group at the start though; some others might wish to do bouldering too!
Please note that we will not teach lead climbing or lead belaying on this event -
we would suggest having some
lessons in Lead Climbing
by a qualified member of staff if this is something you're interested in pursuing!
If you are subsequently unable to attend, please cancel off the event as 'no-shows' are not only rude, but also frustrating for the leader & other attendees who may have travelled over an hour away to climb with you!
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
Indoor climbing centres offer the challenges of climbing that you'll find on natural rock crags - simply indoors! It's a fun way to stay fit, make new friends & develop your climbing skills.
Climbing
- Unlike Indoor Bouldering there is a certain amount of skill to be mastered, such as tying in knots & belaying a partner, as well as the climbs being higher than in bouldering. If you are new to climbing or would like a refresher, then this is just for you!! If you’ve climbed before, can safely tie into a harness & can competently belay, then there’s plenty of choices of top-rope & lead climbing on offer here.
Bouldering
- Instead of tackling long high routes, the 'problems' (as they are referred to) are shorter & focus on technique, balance, body positioning & sometimes power. With the different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, so it’s excellent (but not necessarily easier) for newcomers.
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
has more than 75 lines with over 300 routes, set through some spectacular ground including its notorious 'stalactite'. It even features one of the few indoor 'Yorkshire VS cracks' in the country, to test your jamming skills. The bouldering rooms are just as interesting as its climbing routes, over 200 bouldering problems have been organised into graded circuits to provide something for everyone.

Title: Humps and Bumps: the Clent Hills
Summary:
Hill Walk: 8 miles, 383m ascent. Autumn woods and fabulous views!
Welcome to a new series of walks exploring the humps and bumps of the Central region! Humps are hills with more than 100 metres prominence, and bumps are bulges which protrude a little less. You can find out more about humps
here
. Expect one or two quips on the way round!
The Clent Hills include Walton Hill, at 315m a prominent Hump. Our route begins at Nimmings Wood car park, from where we ascend gradually to the Four Stones viewpoint. The stones look like something from prehistoric times, but were actually erected in the 1750s by Lord Lyttleton of Hagley Hall. The view from here is outstanding on a clear day, particularly to the South West, all the way to the Malverns, Cotswolds and even the Brecon Beacons.
Passing Clent Hill 309m, we descend then ascend the second of the main summits which is slightly higher, Walton Hill at 315m. This is our Hump for today! Walton Hill has fine views especially East towards the Birmingham skyline. Views continue as we follow the top of the ridge south to Calcot Hill, then take the track west.
The woods here include fine, historic woodland and traditional species, particularly oaks, beech, birch and hazel, and a wide variety of fungi in autumn. You may see deer hiding in the woods too!
Lunch stop is just over half way at the top of Clent village. Here, there is a grassy slope good for picnics, the Four Stones café and the Hill Tavern. We are 1 mile from the car park here, so if you wish to take a short cut back that is possible.
In the afternoon, we tackle a bump. A gentle, ancient track takes us to Hagley, where we cross the main road and ascend Wychbury Hill, a bump. It is a fine bump with an obelisk on the top. There are prominent views back over Clent and across Worcestershire.
This is a hill walk with good paths, totally 8 miles with 383m ascent. Find the route
here
. Well behaved dogs are welcome on this walk. If you have any questions, please send the event leader a message.

Title: Gravel Cycling - The White Peak
Summary:
A leisurely cycle in the White Peak area of the Peak District
We will ride a mixture off-road trails, quiet single track lanes and  a short short section of main road.
The route will take us down Long Dale to Hartington before joining the Manifold Trail (former rail line) to Wetton Mill, where we face a stiff climb out of the Manifold Valley to  Wetton Village and a proposed cafe stop for refreshments.
We then head east following quiet lanes and an offroad bridleways through Beresford Dale to cross the River Dove before climbing up to join the Tissington Trail, a former railway route now converted to  a very popular route for both walkers and cyclists.
The Tissington Trail climbs gradually all the way to the Northern End close to the end of the ride.
Ride is approximately
40km with 600m of climbing
For this ride, Mountain Bike, Road, Gravel or Hybrid bike is suitable, surfaces are good on the off road sections.
Whilst the ascent may appear significant, we have plenty of time to take the climbs slowly and we will ride at the pace of the slowest, wait at the top of climbs, none of the climbs are excessively steep, but should you need to walk, no one we be left behind.
Should you have any questions about the route please message the leader.

At the end of the walk, we can head to the

Title: Leisure Cycle - Anderton Boat Lift & Whitegate Way
Summary:
A leisurely social bike
ride
along lanes of the Cheshire Countryside, and a cafe stop at Whitegate Station.
We ride a loop around Northwich Conurbation passing the Anderton Boat Lift and several pretty Cheshire Villages following mainly follow quiet lanes, and approximately 10 miles on a former Railway Line (Whitegate Way) and Bridleway.   We can stop for coffee and cake at the former station House on the Whitegate Way. After passing through Knutsford, we will pass through Tatton Park.
This event is around 36
miles
and is reasonably flat.  Whilst the majority of the route is on traffic free trails or quiet lanes, please note we do route along a few sections of busy roads to access the Boat Lift and will pass through Knutsford Town Centre on some busier roads.
We have plenty of time to complete the route and we will take it at a relaxed pace and no one will be left behind.
Road cyclists:
Please be aware some paths might be a little rough and bumpy for thin tyres, but doable none the less.  some sections of mud can be expected on the trails.
Mountain bikers:
Much of the route is on paved roads and expect to mix with traffic.
Pace and Terrain
This will be a leisurely cycle suitable for those of all levels of fitness. The majority of the route is on quiet country lanes, but we do have about 10 miles on the old railway line which can be muddy in places, but suitable for all bikes.
This event is open to cyclists of all abilities and bike types. There are a couple of climbs as we cross the Weaver Valley a couple of times.
If you're not a regular cyclist, please do make sure your bike is in good condition - check the tyres are well inflated, chain is oiled, and you've got a spare inner tube, drinks and snacks with you.
Photos:
All were taken by the Author.
Difficulty & Distance: Approximately 60km with 350m ascent

Title: Roughing It Alongside The Cotswolds Set
Summary:
Overview:
When I alighted at Charlbury station for the recce, I was greeted by a mêlée of people dressed head-to-toe in Barbour, animatedly discussing whether they were having crab or lobster for lunch, washed down with their Prosecco. It turned out that a local horse trials was taking place, and a convoy of fancy, branded 4x4s soon whisked them off towards Cornbury House. That left me free to enjoy a quieter corner of the Cotswolds fringes — just far enough from Diddly Squat and the assorted ‘celebrities’ - David Cameron, Elisabeth Murdoch, Rebekah Brooks, Jeremy Clarkson and Ellen DeGeneres - to name a few of the 'charming' glitterati who have made the Chipping Norton area their home, and rather than exploring the countryside and local pubs are more likely to frequent the Soho Farmhouse to keep themselves amused.
Starting from
Charlbury Station
, this circular adventure heads out into quiet Cotswolds fringes Oxfordshire countryside, with rolling fields, country lanes and plenty of four-legged locals along the way – expect sheep, horses and cows. Halfway around, we’ll reach
Church Enstone
, where we'll stop for lunch and have the option to have a drink at The Crown pub.
The return leg takes us through the grounds and surroundings of
Ditchley Park
, adding a touch of grandeur to proceedings.
A proper countryside walk with plenty of fresh air, great scenery, good company and, naturally, a healthy dose of OutdoorLads banter. 🍻🌳🐑
Route:
From Charlbury Station, we’ll take a short stroll into the town centre, with its honey-stone buildings and impressive church, before heading north-west across open fields dotted with sheep. We’ll pass Coldron Mill before approaching the small village of Spelsbury, where its distinctive squat church tower comes into view as we arrive.
From Spelsbury, the route continues through woodland and across more open countryside, passing the hamlet of Lidstone before joining the Shakespeare’s Way. After crossing the A44, we’ll reach our half way lunch stop in the small village of Church Enstone, home to a village pub and another impressive church.
After lunch, we’ll head south, following sections of the Shakespeare’s Way before skirting woodland and eventually reaching the grounds of Ditchley Park. Here, we’ll enjoy some parkland walking and get a glimpse of the impressive façade of Ditchley House.
Once we leave the estate, there are just a couple of miles to go before we return to Charlbury, entering the town from the north. Depending on train times, there may be an opportunity for a well-earned post-walk drink in one of the town’s pubs. From the town centre, it’s only a 10-minute stroll back to Charlbury Station — making this a walk with countryside, history, a decent lunch and, potentially, a final drink before heading home.
The route can be found
here
:
The Sites:
Charlbury
is a historic Cotswold town on the River Evenlode, surrounded by attractive countryside and woodland. Its compact centre features traditional honey-coloured stone buildings, the impressive 15th-century Church of St Mary the Virgin and the historic Market Street. The town also has a long connection with the local wool and glove-making industries.
Spelsbury
is a small Cotswold village centred around its distinctive
St Mary the Virgin Church
, whose squat stone tower is a prominent landmark. Its name is thought to derive from Old English, meaning “Spelle’s fortified place”.
Church Enstone
is a small Cotswold village situated in the valley of the River Glyme. It is centred around St Kenelm’s Church, a historic parish church with origins dating back to the medieval period. The name Enstone is thought to derive from the Old English
Enna’s tūn
, meaning “Enna’s settlement”.
Ditchley Park
is a historic country estate set within around 3,000 acres of parkland, woodland and farmland. The present Ditchley House was built in the early 18th century for George Lee, 2nd Earl of Lichfield, and is noted for its grand Baroque architecture and landscaped grounds. The estate has an interesting political history: during the Second World War, Winston Churchill used Ditchley Park as an alternative country retreat when security concerns made Chequers less suitable. Today, the house is privately owned and used as a venue for conferences, retreats and private events.
The
Shakespeare’s Way
is a long-distance walking trail of around 146 miles (235 km) linking Shakespeare’s birthplace in Stratford-upon-Avon with Shakespeare’s Globe in London. In Oxfordshire, the trail passes through the Cotswolds and its fringes and this walk includes sections of it.
Dogs:
Well-behaved dogs are welcome, there will be a few areas where we are walking along or crossing roads but the majority of the walk is in open countryside where dogs can be let off the lead, however there will be some fields with horses, cows and sheep where dogs will need to be on leads. Please abide by the Countryside Code (
https://tinyurl.com/rlqvp3h
) and remember not everyone loves dogs as much as you do so be mindful of other members.
Photos:
All photos the leader's own (taken in Sept 2026 so not necessarily representative of conditions in mid November!), with permission given to OutdoorLads for use.
Difficulty & Distance: 12.8 miles, generally good condition paths of grass, dirt and tarmac, moderately undulating with a total ascent of 300 meters

Title: Autumnal Ashurst Ramble Round Lyndhurst
Summary:
This walk and its write-up are largely based on the assessment walk led by the lovely
Patrick Revell
back in February 2023.
This circular walk from Ashurst Railway Station explores the timeless landscapes of ancient native woodland and open heathland in the New Forest. The
route
visits the small villages of Emery Down and Bank on the outskirts of Lyndhurst, both of which have traditional pubs.
Throughout the day, we will see plenty of the iconic New Forest ponies, quite likely some cattle and donkeys, and possibly also some families of pigs out foraging freely, as we will be visiting during 'pannage season' when pigs are turned out into the Forest to hoover up the fallen acorns which can be poisonous to the ponies and cattle.
The first part of the walk follows the sinuous course of Bartley Water. Here there are fine examples of oxbow lakes that have formed (or are in the process of forming) where the river cuts off its own bends as its course evolves over time. There are numerous impressive Douglas fir trees growing along the riverbanks here, planted in 1864, among the tallest trees in the New Forest.
After crossing the A337 the route passes through chestnut woodland, then follows a bridleway into Emery Down. From here we'll climb to the top of Lyndhurst Hill and pause for lunch. Despite its prominence over the surrounding landscape, I can't promise extensive views, as the hill is covered in a dense oak, beech and birch woodland. After a steep descent we'll cross the A35 to the small hamlet of Bank, and take the opportunity to call in at The Oak Inn, built in the 1850s.
From Bank we start to heading back towards Ashurst, initially along about a mile of gravel cycle paths before branching off-piste into far more interesting open-access ancient native woodland, crossing under the A337 via an underpass, and continuing through more fine woodland and open tightly-grazed lawns. As we emerge out of the woodland we'll pass by Limewood Hotel, one of the Forest's highest rated hotels, which has hosted many celebrity functions including the weddings of Noel Gallagher and Jamie Cullum (although not to each other!)
The final couple of miles are across open heather-clad heathland, crossing the fledgling Beaulieu River, and back into Ashurst. The New Forest pub is right by the station, and offers food and drink for those of us who are in no rush to head home.
Dogs
well-behaved dogs are welcome on the walk, but must be under close control at all times and on a lead in the vicinity of livestock or where wildlife may be disturbed. Also note that the majority of this walk will be in areas where livestock is free-roaming including many areas of dense but vast woodland. Your dog will be aware of nearby animals long before you are, and so you will need to confident that your dog will remain under control otherwise it could be gone for a VERY long time if it starts a chase.
Don’t Waste That Space!
Walks can get filled up quite quickly, so please only sign up if you know you are free to attend. Plans do sometimes change, but remember to free up your space so someone else can attend. If there is a waiting list, please sign up, as spaces often become available closer to the date.
New Members:
If this is your first event or you are new to OutdoorLads we’d love to see you. Please message me if you have any questions.
All images used on this page taken by the event leader and permission granted for use by ODL
Difficulty & Distance: Distance is 17 km (10.5 miles); total ascent is 160 m (525 feet); relief is gently undulating; terrain is dirt, grass, gravel and tarmac.

Title: BIRMINGHAM Indoor Climbing - MONDAY - Experienced
Summary:
Join OutdoorLads for an evening at Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre.
"EXPERIENCED" in this instance is those that have previously climbed & can answer YES to all three of these questions:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie in to a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay another climber correctly & confidently?
Please ensure you only sign up for this event if you
satisfy all three of the prerequisites as an experienced (independent) climber!
Never climbed before? Need a refresher on the basics? Answered NO to any of the three questions above? You will need to
attend one of the beginners (supervised) events
instead, where we will happily sign you in to be supervised (two people per leader maximum), show you the ropes & teach you everything you need to know to climb safely! Beginner (supervised) events are not offered every week.
If you are climbing with us for the first time, whether Experienced or Beginner, it is essential that you send a note to the Event Leader telling them about your previous climbing experience & your goals!
Bouldering
- Most of us do roped climbing, but if you prefer to do bouldering, you can sign yourself in & go bouldering (unsupervised) instead of, or as well as, roped climbing. Please meet the leader & the group at the start though; some others might wish to do bouldering too!
Please note that we will not teach lead climbing or lead belaying on this event -
we would suggest having some
lessons in Lead Climbing
by a qualified member of staff if this is something you're interested in pursuing!
If you are subsequently unable to attend, please cancel off the event as 'no-shows' are not only rude, but also frustrating for the leader & other attendees who may have travelled over an hour away to climb with you!
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
Indoor climbing centres offer the challenges of climbing that you'll find on natural rock crags - simply indoors! It's a fun way to stay fit, make new friends & develop your climbing skills.
Climbing
- Unlike Indoor Bouldering there is a certain amount of skill to be mastered, such as tying in knots & belaying a partner, as well as the climbs being higher than in bouldering. If you are new to climbing or would like a refresher, then this is just for you!! If you’ve climbed before, can safely tie into a harness & can competently belay, then there’s plenty of choices of top-rope & lead climbing on offer here.
Bouldering
- Instead of tackling long high routes, the 'problems' (as they are referred to) are shorter & focus on technique, balance, body positioning & sometimes power. With the different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, so it’s excellent (but not necessarily easier) for newcomers.
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
has more than 75 lines with over 300 routes, set through some spectacular ground including its notorious 'stalactite'. It even features one of the few indoor 'Yorkshire VS cracks' in the country, to test your jamming skills. The bouldering rooms are just as interesting as its climbing routes, over 200 bouldering problems have been organised into graded circuits to provide something for everyone.
You MUST register via this event page before coming to the centre!
To climb, you will need to:
Complete a
Registration Form
(please arrive early to do this in-person the first time) & pay a Registration Fee:
Annual Registration
is
£5
or
Day Registration
is
£3
Pay an
Entry Fee
directly to the climbing centre:
Standard Entry
is
£12.50
&
Bouldering Only
is
£8.50.
Hire
climbing shoes (
£3.50
) & a climbing harness (
£3.50
) if you don't own your own.
Please see Redpoint's
website
for current prices & note that prices are subject to change.
If you have any questions or need any more information just get in touch with the event leader by clicking on their profile below, or take a look at the
My first climbing event page
for more information.
PLEASE NOTE:
All those attending the event must also be aware of the climbing centre's own terms & conditions of participation & abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre's staff.
Photos:
taken & used with permission of
R. Casabuena
&
K. Jones
.
Difficulty & Distance: This event is for EXPERIENCED (independent) climbers only!!!

Title: Xmas Bristol Indoor Bouldering Special - all abilities welcome!
Summary:
The Climbing Academy is one of the best bouldering centres in the South West. With over 200 problems in a 750 square metre area there is enough to keep even the avid of boulderers occupied.
Bouldering is a form of climbing where instead of long high routes, the 'problems' as they are referred to tend to be shorter and focus on technique, balance, body positioning and sometimes power. Because of this different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, harnesses and belaying, which makes the activities excellent for newcomers to the sport. For this reason, it is often regarded as the 'purest' form of climbing.
If you're a seasoned climber you won't need convincing about the benefits of bouldering, but for those who've never climbed more than a staircase, the benefits are wide ranging: from the physical - improved strength, tone, balance, power and coordination; mental - problem solving, focus, concentration and body awareness; to the emotional - relaxation, a sense of achievement and a feeling that mind and body are working together perfectly ('feeling psyched'). On top of all this, bouldering tends to be a very social sport where you can hang out with mates and each have a go as you feel regardless of what level you climb at.
This event is for members of all levels of experience and all are welcome to come along to any of the sessions.
To come along, you will need to register via the event page, and to climb you will need to pay an entry fee directly to the centre when you arrive. For entry fee prices go to:
https://www.theclimbingacademy.com/prices/
. As we start at 8pm you will pay the off-peak price.
For your first time climbing with us, especially if you are a novice climber, please contact the event leader in advance to let him know what your skills and experience are.
It is important that all members sign up through the event page to make sure the event leader has all information of the members attending.
Climbing and Bouldering Participation statement
Please note that every person participating should be aware of (and accept) that those members perceived as ‘in charge’ or leading the event are not necessarily qualified, do not need to be qualified, and are not regarded by OutdoorLads, or themselves as ‘technical experts’ but are amateur climbers with experience and who are happy to impart their knowledge. Any advice given should be considered with this in mind by the recipient.
All those attending the event must also be aware of the centre's own terms and conditions of participation and abide by them, along with any instructions given by the centre's staff. Everyone must also take responsibility for their own safety while participating in Indoor climbing events.

Title: Matlock Bath to Ambergate - DVH Way Section 5
Summary:
The Derwent Valley Trust
was set up in 1996 to promote the history, arts, wildlife and leisure opportunities that surround the river Derwent along its 55 mile course through Derbyshire.
The Derwent Valley Heritage Way
takes us from Ladybower Reservoir in the Peak District National Park to its end at Derwent Mouth where it flows into the River Trent near Shardlow. The Duke of Devonshire opened the walk at Chatsworth House in 2003.
The route takes us through the Chatsworth estate, Derbyshire dales, towns, villages, canals and many points of interests through the
Derwent Valley Mills World Heritage Site
. There are plenty of pubs and tea shops for refreshments along the way. The route follows the riverside path through Derby City and continues southeastwards to the historic inland port of Shardlow. Journey’s end is at Derwent Mouth where the Derwent flows into the River Trent.
The route is divided into eight sections of between  ~13 km (8 miles) and ~17 km (10.5 miles), each with a clear public transport solution. All, except the first section, are linear routes. We park at the end, travel to the start, and walk back to our cars. Sections 5, 6, 7 are brilliantly served by the East Midlands Railway Derwent Valley Line
(Derby–Matlock, hourly), which runs almost parallel to the trail the whole way. For sections (2, 3, 4 and 8), we use local buses.
Each section is a walk in itself. Join one or more, as you wish, or walk all eight sections to complete the whole route through Derbyshire. Please ask other attendees for a lift if you need one.
Section 5 – Matlock Bath to Ambergate
~
13.5 km (8.4 miles) Total ascent 210 m (689 ft)
From the station we see the cable cars that take visitors up to the Heights of Abraham on the other side of the Derwent. Matlock Bath is a former spa town, now a popular holiday destination for motorcyslists and other tourists. It feels rather like a land-locked seaside town!
Masson Mills
working Textiles Museum is the finest surviving and best preserved example of a Richard Arkwright cotton spinning mill with 100-year-old working looms, water turbines and ‘Titanic’ steam boilers.
From the mill we climb up through ancient woodlands at Harp Edge to Cromford, where Arkwright built rows of houses for his mill-workers.
Scarthin bookshop
has a huge stock of old books and local interest titles.
We climb Scarthin Rock to view Akwright's former family home of Willersley Castle and take a look at the
Cromford Mills
visitor attraction. Along the Cromford Canal, at High Peak Junction, railway workshops have been faithfully restored to how they would have looked in the 1880s, and a visitor centre provides information about this historic transport hub.
We skirt the bottom of Lea Wood from where we can see the impressive
Leawood Pumphouse
, maintained and operated by volunteers. We follow the disused Cromford Canal - a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and local nature reserve - through Gregory's tunnel and Whatstandwell between Crich Chase and Shining Cliff Wood back to Ambergate station.
At the end of the walk, there is an opportunity to take refreshments at The Hurt Arms pub.
Well behaved
dogs are welcome
but must kept under control at all times.

Title: BIRMINGHAM Indoor Climbing - MONDAY - Experienced
Summary:

"EXPERIENCED" in this instance is those that have previously climbed & can answer YES to all three of these questions:
Can you fit a climbing harness correctly?
Can you tie in to a rope using the correct knots?
Can you belay another climber correctly & confidently?
Please ensure you only sign up for this event if you
satisfy all three of the prerequisites as an experienced (independent) climber!
Never climbed before? Need a refresher on the basics? Answered NO to any of the three questions above? You will need to
attend one of the beginners (supervised) events
instead, where we will happily sign you in to be supervised (two people per leader maximum), show you the ropes & teach you everything you need to know to climb safely! Beginner (supervised) events are not offered every week.
If you are climbing with us for the first time, whether Experienced or Beginner, it is essential that you send a note to the Event Leader telling them about your previous climbing experience & your goals!
Bouldering
- Most of us do roped climbing, but if you prefer to do bouldering, you can sign yourself in & go bouldering (unsupervised) instead of, or as well as, roped climbing. Please meet the leader & the group at the start though; some others might wish to do bouldering too!
Please note that we will not teach lead climbing or lead belaying on this event -
we would suggest having some
lessons in Lead Climbing
by a qualified member of staff if this is something you're interested in pursuing!
If you are subsequently unable to attend, please cancel off the event as 'no-shows' are not only rude, but also frustrating for the leader & other attendees who may have travelled over an hour away to climb with you!
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
Indoor climbing centres offer the challenges of climbing that you'll find on natural rock crags - simply indoors! It's a fun way to stay fit, make new friends & develop your climbing skills.
Climbing
- Unlike Indoor Bouldering there is a certain amount of skill to be mastered, such as tying in knots & belaying a partner, as well as the climbs being higher than in bouldering. If you are new to climbing or would like a refresher, then this is just for you!! If you’ve climbed before, can safely tie into a harness & can competently belay, then there’s plenty of choices of top-rope & lead climbing on offer here.
Bouldering
- Instead of tackling long high routes, the 'problems' (as they are referred to) are shorter & focus on technique, balance, body positioning & sometimes power. With the different emphasis, bouldering doesn't have the hassle of climbing with ropes, so it’s excellent (but not necessarily easier) for newcomers.
Redpoint Birmingham Climbing Centre
has more than 75 lines with over 300 routes, set through some spectacular ground including its notorious 'stalactite'. It even features one of the few indoor 'Yorkshire VS cracks' in the country, to test your jamming skills. The bouldering rooms are just as interesting as its climbing routes, over 200 bouldering problems have been organised into graded circuits to provide something for everyone.
